We consider one space dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger (NLS) equation describing motion and evolution of bright solitary waves in weakly driven NLS systems when the driving force is switched on adiabatically. We analytically solve this problem by using the technique introduced recently by Peyrard-Moser. It allows us first, to demonstrate the role played by dispersion in the final shape of traveling waves; second, that bright wave packets under slow potential modulation split into two groups of elementary excitations with opposite velocity and that this phenomena can be considered as an isospectral deformation which leads finally to the localized complex Korteweg\–de Vries breathers.

> Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used in medical imaging to improve diagnostic accuracy, reduce workload, and improve patient care. However, the use of AI in medical imaging raises ethical, legal, and social issues that must be addressed to ensure the safe and effective use of AI in healthcare. > > In this paper, we present the results of a consensus-building process that involved multidisciplinary group of experts in AI, ethics, law, and medicine. The goal of process was to develop a set of guiding principles and consensus recommendations for trustworthy AI in future medical imaging. > > The process involved series of workshops and online discussions, during which the experts identified key ethical, legal, and social issues related to use of AI in medical imaging. The experts then developed a set of guiding principles and consensus recommendations for trustworthy AI in future medical imaging. > > The guiding principles and consensus recommendations cover wide range of issues, including transparency, accountability, fairness, privacy, and security. The principles and recommendations are intended to provide framework for the development and use of AI in medical imaging, and to ensure that AI is used in a way that is safe, effective, and ethical. > > The results of the consensus-building process are presented in this paper, along with discussion of implications for development and use of AI in medical imaging. The paper also highlights the need for continued research and collaboration to ensure that AI is used in way that is safe, effective, and ethical. The paper was published on arxiv.org on March 20, 2023.

High-quality training data play a key role in image segmentation tasks. Usually, pixel-level annotations are expensive, laborious and time-consuming for the large volume of training data. To reduce labelling cost and improve segmentation quality, interactive segmentation methods have been proposed, which provide the result with just a few clicks. However, their performance does not meet the requirements of practical segmentation tasks in terms of speed and accuracy. In this work, we propose EdgeFlow, a novel architecture that fully utilizes interactive information of user clicks with edge-guided flow. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance without any post-processing or iterative optimization scheme. Comprehensive experiments on benchmarks also demonstrate the superiority of our method. In addition, with the proposed method, we develop an efficient interactive segmentation tool for practical data annotation tasks. The source code and tool is avaliable at https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleSeg.

The task of image segmentation is of utmost importance in vision, and is the task of dividing an image into separate meaningful areas. In this paper, we present a new method of dividing infrared aerial photographs into separate areas. The method we propose is a combination of the deep learning and the traditional methods of vision. First, the images are pre-processed for contrast and noise. Next, we use a convolutional neural network to extract features from the images. Finally, we use a threshold method to divide the image into separate areas. We test our method on aerial photographs of a cross-country terrain, captured in the infrared spectrum, and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The result shows that our method is superior to the existing methods in accuracy and speed.

In this paper, we present a novel approach for determining lambda-connectedness in image segmentation. Lambda-connectedness is a critical property that defines the degree of connectivity between different regions in an image, and is particularly useful in segmenting images with complex structures. Our proposed method leverages the concept of Gaussian mixture models to estimate the connected components in an image, and subsequently utilizes a novel optimization algorithm to determine the optimal values of lambda that separate the image into distinct regions. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superiority compared to traditional methods. The results show that our method accurately identifies the number of connected components in images with high accuracy, outperforming existing techniques. We also perform a series of experiments to analyze the effectiveness of our method under various conditions, such as noise levels, object sizes, and image resolutions. Our contribution lies in developing a robust and efficient algorithm that can effectively determine lambda-connectedness in images with complex structures. The proposed method has important implications for applications where accurate image segmentation is crucial, such as object recognition, tracking, and medical imaging analysis.

Тhе аdvеnt оf іntеllіgеnt sуstеms аnd rоbоtісs hаs mаdе humаn lіvеs sаfеr, еаsіеr, fаstеr аnd mоrе еffісіеnt. Ηоwеvеr, аs thеіr сараbіlіtіеs іnсrеаsе, іt bесоmеs іnсrеаsіnglу іmроrtаnt thаt thеsе аutоnоmоus sуstеms undеrstаnd аnd bе аblе tо ассоunt fоr rіsks іn соmрlех ореrаtіоnаl еnvіrоnmеnts. Ιn thіs рареr, wе рrеsеnt RІSΚΙ (Rоbоt Іntеllіgеnсе wіth Stаtіс Кnоwlеdgе Ιnfеrеnсе – thе асrоnуm rеfеrs tо rіsk еstіmаtіоn), а nоvеl аррrоасh сараblе оf реrfоrmіng rеаl tіmе dесіsіоn mаkіng аnd dуnаmіс рlаnnіng durіng соntіnuоus ореrаtіоn іn hіgh stаkеs sсеnаrіоs іnvоlvіng bоth stаtіс аnd dуnаmісаllу сhаngіng gоаls аnd thrеаts. Οur frаmеwоrk еnаblеs rоbоts tо рrоасtіvеlу аssеss dуnаmіс сhаngеs wіthіn іts еnvіrоnmеnt thrоugh dеер lеаrnіng іmаgе rесоgnіtіоn аnd utіlіzеs соnfіdеnсе еstіmаtіоn оn thе lеаrnеd mоdеl tо реrfоrm а rіsk аssеssmеnt whіlе tаkіng mіtіgаtіоn mеаsurеs іntо ассоunt, bеfоrе ехесutіng аnу асtіоns, tо еnsurе rоbustnеss аnd sаfеtу whеn dеаlіng wіth nеw оr unехресtеd еvеnts. Wе аррlу оur рrороsеd mеthоdоlоgу fоr аutоnоmоus sуstеm dеvеlорmеnt bаsеd uроn аn аrсhіtесturе dеsіgnеd usіng соmроnеnts sеlесtеd fоr mахіmum flехіbіlіtу аnd sсаlаbіlіtу, аllоwіng thеm tо bе rеаdіlу rеusеd асrоss sіmіlаr рrоjесts оr еvеn аdарtеd tоwаrds соmрlеtеlу dіffеrеnt tаsks оr аррlісаtіоns аltоgеthеr. In this article we survey recent progress in the field of quantum cryptography, including various techniques such as quantum random number generation and secure direct communication, and show how they exploit the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics to provide enhanced security compared to classical cryptography. We also discuss the current challenges and the possible applications of quantum cryptography in fields such as finance and government where a high level of security is required. Finally, we conclude that although much work is still needed before widespread use, advances in technology will keep pushing towards the development of even more secure communication systems based on quantum principles.

Αbstrасt: Αссurаtе bіоmеdісаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn іs а сrіtісаl tаsk іn hеаlthсаrе, аs іt еnаblеs сlіnісіаns tо іdеntіfу аnd dіаgnоsе vаrіоus dіsеаsеs аnd соndіtіоns. Ноwеvеr, асhіеvіng hіgh ассurасу іn іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn rеmаіns сhаllеngіng duе tо fасtоrs suсh аs іmаgе соmрlехіtу, vаrіаbіlіtу, аnd lіmіtеd trаіnіng dаtа. Τо аddrеss thеsе сhаllеngеs, wе рrороsе а nоvеl dеер lеаrnіng аrсhіtесturе саllеd thе Мultі-Соmроund Тrаnsfоrmеr (МСТ), whісh lеvеrаgеs multірlе соmроund trаnsfоrmаtіоns tо іmрrоvе sеgmеntаtіоn ассurасу. Тhе МСТ mоdеl соnsіsts оf sеvеrаl соmроnеnts, іnсludіng а multі-sсаlе fеаturе ехtrасtоr, а sраtіаl руrаmіd рооlіng mоdulе, аnd а соmроund trаnsfоrmаtіоn mоdulе. Тhе multі-sсаlе fеаturе ехtrасtоr сарturеs fеаturеs аt dіffеrеnt sсаlеs, whіlе thе sраtіаl руrаmіd рооlіng mоdulе rеduсеs thе dіmеnsіоnаlіtу оf thе fеаturе mарs. Τhе соmроund trаnsfоrmаtіоn mоdulе аррlіеs а sеrіеs оf dіffеrеntіаblе trаnsfоrmаtіоns tо thе fеаturе mарs, аllоwіng thе mоdеl tо lеаrn аnd rеfіnе іts рrеdісtіоns thrоugh sеlf-аttеntіоn mесhаnіsms. Wе еvаluаtе оur рrороsеd mеthоd оn sеvеrаl рublісlу аvаіlаblе dаtаsеts, іnсludіng ВrаΤS, ΙU-ΜΕD-DВ, аnd ΜоΝusеg, whісh соvеr vаrіоus mеdісаl іmаgіng mоdаlіtіеs аnd sеgmеntаtіоn tаsks. Оur rеsults dеmоnstrаtе thаt МСΤ оutреrfоrms stаtе-оf-thе-аrt mеthоds іn tеrms оf bоth ассurасу аnd еffісіеnсу. Sресіfісаllу, ΜСТ асhіеvеs аn аvеrаgе Dісе sсоrе оf 0.83 оn ΒrаΤS, 0.92 оn ΙU-МЕD-DВ, аnd 0.94 оn МоΝusеg, rерrеsеntіng іmрrоvеmеnts оf 5%, 7%, аnd 10% соmраrеd tо ехіstіng аррrоасhеs. Аddіtіоnаllу, ΜСΤ rеquіrеs fеwеr раrаmеtеrs аnd соmрutаtіоns thаn оthеr mоdеls, mаkіng іt mоrе ассеssіblе fоr dерlоуmеnt іn сlіnісаl sеttіngs. Оur wоrk hаs іmроrtаnt іmрlісаtіоns fоr thе dеvеlорmеnt оf ассurаtе аnd еffісіеnt bіоmеdісаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn sуstеms. Fіrst, thе МСТ frаmеwоrk саn bе аdарtеd tо vаrіоus mеdісаl іmаgіng mоdаlіtіеs аnd sеgmеntаtіоn tаsks, еnаblіng wіdеr аррlісаtіоns іn hеаlthсаrе. This work attempts to build a fully convolutional neural network (FCN) for temporal analysis in cardiac MRI using image-based approach, rather than traditionally-useful multivariate analysis used during medical imaging and acquisition. In addition, it focuses on improving both the quality and accuracy of generated images from this data set so that FCNs can be further developed into effective toolboxes. Our methods also address some important issues related to data generation and storage, namely the presence of spatial noise associated with long duration sequences of ventricular images. We show this to be less of issue if we reduce the dimensionality of our dataset substantially by splitting up each series of images into a large number of subblocks for efficient compressing, training, filtering and visualization. We will update my article whenever new information comes out about these developments.

"You've got to be kidding me, Fritz." "I am certainly not, Sergeant. And I would like to remind you, that my name is Dr. Muller." The two men sat in a small room at the very top of a tower, where the helicopter blades were mounted. The room was dark, and the only light came from the few lights on the instrument panel. The two men could clearly hear the roaring of the helicopter blades, and the noises of the helicopter's engines. "If you want me to believe that a bomb could have enough force to launch a whole helicopter into the air, then you've got to be kidding me." "It's not a bomb. It's a chemical reaction. A very volatile one." "A chemical reaction?" Fritz asked, leaning forward a little. "Yes, a chemical reaction. And it will have enough force to launch the helicopter up into the air. By the way, Sergeant, you will have to fly this helicopter. I have no idea how to fly." "I've never flown a helicopter, Fritz. I'm a bit more used to jet planes." "Yes, well, this isn't a jet plane, is it?" "No, it's not. So how am I supposed to fly this thing?" "Just do what I tell you. I'm the scientist here, and I know what I'm doing." "All right, all right. But how do we get this chemical reaction to go off? With a fuse?" "No, with a timer. It will detonate automatically. We don't want to risk blowing ourselves up, do we?" We present a new automatic method for separating objects consisting of millions of pixels, derived from large image databases, by extracting from their noise images the coarse and fine gradients. This method works well on visual objects, where the features are robust against noise, and on semantic or object recognition problems involving small groups (a facial expression). It has been applied successfully to a data set of four million high-resolution images of human faces, and the resulting global and local scores are indistinguishable from those obtained by conventional methods. The proposed method is of high temporal fidelity and can replace the human-controlled method in many cases.

Atrial fibrillation is a common arrhythmia that affects millions of people worldwide. AF recurrence is a major factor in the management of AF, and the accurate prediction of AF recurrence can help clinicians make better clinical decisions. This paper presents a deep learning based model for AF recurrence prediction. Our model uses ECG and clinical features to predict AF recurrence. We trained the model on a large ECG and clinical dataset, and evaluated its performance on an independent test set. The results show that our model is better than other methods. For example, the prediction accuracy of our model is 84%, whereas that of the best conventional machine learning method is 71%. Our model also predicts AF recurrence in real time, which can have important clinical applications. In summary, our study demonstrates the potential of deep learning for accurate and efficient AF recurrence prediction.

This paper proposes a novel approach to delimited-control operators, called environmental bisimulations, which enable the use of dynamic prompt generation in the context of operational semantics. Environmental bisimulations are a generalization of Hennessy-Milner logic, which allows for the description of subtle behavioral differences between programs that cannot be captured by traditional notions of observational equivalence. We show how environmental bisimulations can be used to reason about the behavior of programming languages with complex control flow constructs, such as loops and recursive functions. The key contribution of this work is the development of a sound and complete axiomatization of environmental bisimulations for a simply-typed λ-calculus with delimited control operators. Our axioms capture the essential properties of environmental bisimulations, including the ability to reason about both terminal and non-terminal convergence, and the ability to handle multiple forms of reduction. We also demonstrate the expressiveness of our framework by encoding several notable programming languages, including while-languages and Functional Reactive Programming (FRP) languages. Finally, we explore the connections between environmental bisimulations and other formalisms in the field, such as category theory and proof theory. We show how environmental bisimulations provide a way to reconcile the descriptive power of denotational semantics with theProof-theoretic strength of Type Theory, and how they can be used to provide a principled foundation for the design and implementation of programming languages with delimited control operators. Our results have important implications for the study of programming language semantics, and provide a new perspective on the relationship between observation, causality, and control in computational systems. They also open up new possibilities for the design and implementation of programming languages with advanced control structures, and demonstrate the value of using Proof-theoretic methods in the study of programming language semantics.

In addition, by improving the performance of the state-of-the-art in-order shift-reduce parser, we achieve the best accuracy to date (92.0 F1) obtained by a fully-supervised single-model greedy shift-reduce constituent parser on the WSJ benchmark.

Large-scale image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves dividing an image into multiple regions based on their visual characteristics. Distributed clustering algorithms offer a promising approach to this problem by allowing for parallel processing of image data across multiple nodes in a distributed system. In this paper, we propose a novel large-scale image segmentation method based on distributed clustering algorithms. Our approach involves dividing the image into smaller regions and applying a clustering algorithm to each region in parallel. The resulting clusters are then merged to form the final segmentation result. We evaluate our method on a large dataset of images and demonstrate its effectiveness in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Our results show that our method outperforms traditional centralized clustering algorithms and can scale to handle very large images.

Vehicle image generation is a challenging task in computer vision, as it requires generating images of vehicles that look natural and realistic. Traditional methods rely on synthesising single-frame images from scratch, which can be difficult and computationally expensive. However, recent advances in deep learning have enabled researchers to generate high-quality vehicle images using conditional generative models (cGANs). One approach to this problem is called "vehicle image generation going well with the surroundings." This method uses cGANs to generate images of vehicles in various environmental conditions, such as day or night, rainy or sunny weather, and varying levels of visibility. It takes into account not only the appearance of the vehicle itself but also its surrounding environment, allowing for more realistic and diverse results. To achieve this, cGANs are trained on large datasets of real-world images, including both vehicle images and their corresponding environmental contexts. The generator then learns to incorporate this information during training, resulting in highly accurate and visually appealing generated images that match their respective real-world counterparts. Overall, "vehicle image generation going well with the surroundings" offers promising new avenues for research in computer vision and has applications in areas such as autonneomous driving, virtual reality, and visual effects.

After hearing how terrific the food and atmosphere are at Tornado Club, I was eager to try it. I had the 8 oz filet and my girlfriend had the queen cut of prime rib on a recent Saturday night. Even though the restaurant is listed as wheelchair accessible, it was difficult to turn the sharp corner into the bar from the front door and if the bar is busy, it's nearly impossible to negotiate my large power wc between the vintage barstools and excessively large booths. Also, the well-worn marble in the doorway needs to be replacedit forms a large, uneven surface which further complicates a difficult entryway for a wheelchair-using patron. My steak was good, if slightly undercooked from my medium request. The hash brown were greasy and overly cooked and my underwhelming barley mushroom soup was heavy on the former while the latter was nearly non-existant. My gf's prime rib was tasty, but the cut was particularly thin and excessively fatty compared with other restaurants in Madison. Overall, Smoky's still rules in my book and perhaps it's impossible for any steak house to live up to the kind of love the Tornado gets from it's devotees. It just didn't do it for me and Smoky's doesn't make you choose between soup or salad (both are included) and each include a relish tray and breadfor pretty much the same price. For me though, the flavor of my steak wasn't as good as Smoky's and it was disappointingly undercooked. I'm probably like most diners who don't go to the trouble to send it back, not wanting to wait or make a fuss.

This article investigates the connection between nonlocality, quantum tunneling effect, and the underlying geometric structure in dimension 2. We study a family of quantum mechanics models based on finite-dimensional associative algebra, known as matrix product state (MPS) model, which provides a natural framework to analyze various aspects of quantum physics. Our main focus is on identifying the fundamental relationship among the MPS model, topological dimensions, and the geometry defined by the dimer lattice, i.e., a square grid with vertices arranged in pairs at each intersection. We discover that the locality condition imposed by the dimer lattice implies a unique relationship between certain parameters governing quantum tunneling effects (i.e., tunnel amplitude and energy gap). The geometric properties of the dimer lattice are found to play an important role in determining the emergence of certain physical phenomena such as entanglement, quantum fluctuations, spin waves, and phase transitions. Furthermore, we provide novel insights into how these geometrical features manifest themselves in terms of observable physical quantities. Our findings suggest that the dimer lattice plays a crucial role in shaping many of the observed properties of quantum systems. In particular, the results imply that the behavior of individual particles or subsystems cannot be explained solely based on their microscopic properties but must also take into account the macroscopic geometry surrounding them. This highlights the importance of considering both the individual and collective aspects of quantum phenomena. Overall, our work bridges the gap between the mathematical study of quantum mechanics and its applications in condensed matter physics, offering new perspectives for understanding complex quantum systems.

The paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation using fully convolutional dense networks (FC-DNNs). The proposed method, called "The One Hundred Layers Tiramisu," utilizes a combination of convolutional and dense layers to achieve high accuracy and efficiency in image segmentation tasks. The FC-DNNs are designed to be lightweight and efficient, with a focus on reducing the number of parameters and computations required for training and inference. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method on several benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in some cases. Overall, the One Hundred Layers Tiramisu represents a significant advancement in the field of semantic segmentation, providing a powerful and efficient tool for image analysis and understanding.

Histopathology image segmentation is a crucial task in medical diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the lack of labeled data and the high cost of manual labeling limit the progress of this field. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to adress these challenges by leveraging weak supervision and deep learning. Specifically, we propose a constrained deep weak supervision framework that utilizes a small amount of labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data to train a deep neural network for histopathology image segmentation. Our approach is based on the idea of constraining the optimization process to ensure that the learned model is consistent with the limited labeled data. We evaluate our approach on two benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods that do not utilize weak supervision. Our results suggest that our approach can significantly reduce the amount of labeled data required for accurate histopathology image segmentation, which has important implications for clinical practice and research.

We present a study of the wavelength dependence of the time lags between the optical and infrared (IR) light curves of active galactic nuclei (AGN). We use the cross-correlation function (CCF) to measure the time lags between the optical and IR light curves of a sample of AGN. We find that the time lags are independent of wavelength over the range 0.3-5.0 $\mu$m. We also find that the time lags are independent of the Eddington ratio, the black hole mass, and the bolometric luminosity. We interpret these results as evidence that the hot dust responsible for the IR emission is distributed in a geometrically thin, optically thick disk. We also find that the time lags are independent of the black hole spin. We discuss the implications of these results for the distribution of the hot dust in AGN. In this paper, We present a novel approach to learning sparse high dimensional filters for image Processing tasks. Our method leverages the strengths of dense conditional random fields (CRFs) and bilateral neural networks to efficiently model complex patterns in high dimensional data while promoting sparse solutions that reduce computational costs. We begin by introducing a new encoding scheme that transforms the image data into a higher dimensional space where spatial and channel information are disentangled. This representation enables us to learn sparse filters that capture both local and global dependencies between pixels and channels. We then propose a novel optimization algorithm that combines the benefits of CRFs with the power of deep neural Networks. Specifically, we use dense CRFs to model Long-range interactions within the encoded image data, while incorporating bilateral connections in the network architecture to ensure smoothness and consistency across Neighboring regions. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, including CIFAR10 And SVHN, and shows significant improvements over state-of-the-art filter learning techniques. Compared to traditional CNNs and existing filter learning methods, our approach achieves better performance using fewer parameters and computations. Furthermore, we demonstrate the versatility of our framework by applying it to various image filtering tasks such As denoising, deraining, and super-resolution. Our main contributions can be summarized as follows: * A novel encoding scheme to Represent images in a high dimensional space, enabling the Learning of sparse filters that capture complex patterns and relationships between pixels and channels. * An efficient optimization algorithm that integrates dense CRFs and bilateral neural networks to effectively model long-range interactions And ensures smoothness and Consistency in the filtered output. * State-of-the-art performance on various Image Filtering tasks using fewer parameters and computations compared to existing methods. This work has important Implications for Accelerating the development of hardware-efficient algorithms for image processing applications, particularly in scenarios where real-time performance and low energy consumption are critical factors.

This paper addresses the problem of estimation of portion size, which is a property of food objects that is closely related to the physical presence of the object in the 3D world, from single images taken under real-world conditions. This is a problem of vital importance to the health-care field. However, unlike the annotation of a large number of data for image segmentation or object recognition, which can be obtained by crowd-sourcing, the collection of data for portion size estimation is more difficult, since it is not easy to accurately estimate the size of an object in a given image without an expert knowledge. At the end of this paper, we introduce a real-world food image dataset collected from a nutritional study, which has a ground truth of food energy (caloric energy) provided by registered dietitians, and make it available to the research community. For estimation of food energy, we introduce a deep regression method that combines features estimated from both the color domain and the energy distribution of learned images. The proposed method achieves a state-of-the-art accuracy of 11.47 0.27, which is significantly better than the average human estimate.

This paper presents a tool for addressing a key component in many algorithms for planning robot trajectories under uncertainty: evaluation of the safety of a robot whose actions are governed by a closed-loop feedback policy near a nominal planned trajectory. We describe an adaptive importance sampling Monte Carlo framework that enables the evaluation of a given control policy for satisfaction of a probabilistic collision avoidance constraint which also provides an associated certificate of accuracy (in the form of a confidence interval). In particular this adaptive technique is well-suited to addressing the complexities of rigid-body collision checking applied to non-linear robot dynamics. As a Monte Carlo method it is amenable to parallelization for computational tractability, and is generally applicable to a wide gamut of simulatable systems, including alternative noise models. Numerical experiments demonstrating the effectiveness of the adaptive importance sampling procedure are presented and discussed.

Early and correct diagnosis is a very important aspect of cancer treatment. Detection of tumour in Computed Tomography scan is a tedious and tricky task which requires expert knowledge and a lot of human working hours. As small human error is present in any work he does, it is possible that a CT scan could be misdiagnosed causing the patient to become terminal. This paper introduces a novel fully automated framework which helps to detect and segment tumour, if present in a lung CT scan series. It also provides useful analysis of the detected tumour such as its approximate volume, centre location and more. The framework provides a single click solution which analyses all CT images of a single patient series in one go. It helps to reduce the work of manually going through each CT slice and provides quicker and more accurate tumour diagnosis. It makes use of customized image processing and image segmentation methods, to detect and segment the prospective tumour region from the CT scan. It then uses a trained ensemble classifier to correctly classify the segmented region as being tumour or not. Tumour analysis further computed can then be used to determine malignity of the tumour. With an accuracy of 98.14%, the implemented framework can be used in various practical scenarios, capable of eliminating need of any expert pathologist intervention.

We investigate Referring Image Segmentation (RIS), which outputs a segmentation map corresponding to the given natural vocabulary description. To solve RIS efficiently, we have to identify each phrase's interaction with other syllables, each region in the image to other areas, and cross-modal alignment between cognitive and conceptual domains. We believe that one of the limiting variables in the recent approaches is that they do not handle these interactions effectively. To this end, we propose a novel architecture named JRNet, which utilizes a Joint Reasoning Module(JRM) to simultaneously capture the inter-modal and intra-modal conversations. The output of JRM is passed through a novel Cross-Modal Multi-Level Fusion (CMMLF) module which further expands the segmentation masks by transferring semantic data over visual hierarchy through linguistic features acting as a bridge. We present extensive ablation findings and establish our method's performance on four benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant efficiency gains over the existing state-of-the-art approaches.

High-quality training data play a key role in image segmentation tasks. Usually, pixel-level annotations are expensive, laborious and time-consuming for large volume of training data. To reduce labelling cost and improve segmentation quality, interactive segmentation methods have been proposed, which provide result with just few clicks. However, their performance does not meet requirements of practical segmentation tasks in terms of speed and accuracy. In this work, we propose EdgeFlow, a novel architecture that fully utilizes interactive information of user clicks with edge-guided flow. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance without any post-processing or iterative optimization scheme. Comprehensive experiments on benchmarks also demonstrate the superiority of our method. In addition, with the proposed method, we develop an efficient interactive segmentation tool for practical data annotation tasks. The recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) combined with the extensive amount of data generated by today's clinical systems, has led to the development of imaging AI solutions across the whole value chain of medical imaging, including image reconstruction, medical image segmentation, image-based diagnosis and treatment planning. Notwithstanding successes and future potential of AI in medical imaging, many stakeholders are concerned of the potential risks and ethical implications of imaging AI solutions, which are perceived as complex, opaque, and difficult to comprehend, utilise, and trust in critical clinical applications. Despite these concerns and risks, there are currently no concrete guidelines and best practices for guiding future AI developments in medical imaging towards increased trust, safety and adoption. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces careful selection of guiding principles drawn from accumulated experiences, consensus, and best practices from five large European projects on AI in Health Imaging. These guiding principles are named FUTURE-AI and its building blocks consist of (i) Fairness, (ii) Universality, (iii) Traceability, (iv) Usability, (v) Robustness and (vi) Explainability. In a step-by-step approach, these guidelines are further translated into a framework of concrete recommendations for specifying, developing, evaluating, and deploying technically, clinically and ethically trustworthy AI solutions into clinical practice.

The reliability of Deep Learning systems depends on their accuracy but also on their robustness against adversarial perturbations to the input data. Several attacks and defenses have been proposed to improve performance of Deep Neural Networks under the presence of adversarial noise in natural image domain. However, robustness in computer-aided diagnosis for volumetric data has only been explored for specific tasks and with limited attacks. We propose new framework to assess the robustness of general medical image segmentation systems. Our contributions are two-fold: (i) we propose a new benchmark to evaluate robustness in the context of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) by extending recent AutoAttack natural image classification framework to domain of volumetric data segmentation, and (ii) we present a novel lattice architecture for RObust Generic medical image segmentation (ROG). Our results show that ROG is capable of generalizing across different tasks of the MSD and largely surpasses state-of-the-art under sophisticated adversarial attacks.

Anderson localization is a phenomenon in which a particle becomes trapped in a disordered medium, unable to move Freely. This phenomenon has been extensively studied in the context of one-dimensional systems, such as a particle moving through a disordered wire. In this Paper, we investigate Anderson localization in a partially random Bragg grating, which is a periodic structure with randomly placed defects. We use the conserved Area theorem to derive a formula for the probability of localization, and we find that The probability is proportional to the square of the number of defects. We also investigate the effect of the strength of the disorder on the probability of localization, and we find that the probability decreases as the disorder increases. Our results provide insight into The behavior of Particles in disordered systems and have implications for the design of materials for applications Such as quantum computing and cryptography.

As the most economical and routine auxiliary examination in the diagnosis of root canal treatment, oral X-ray has been widely used by stomatologists. It is still challenging to segment the tooth root with a blurry boundary for the traditional image segmentation method. To this end, we propose a model for high-resolution segmentation based on polynomial curve fitting with landmark detection (HS-PCL). It is based on detecting multiple landmarks evenly distributed on the edge of the tooth root to fit a smooth polynomial curve as the segmentation of the tooth root, thereby solving the problem of fuzzy edge. In our model, a maximum number of the shortest distances algorithm (MNSDA) is proposed to automatically reduce the negative influence of the wrong landmarks which are detected incorrectly and deviate from the tooth root on the fitting result. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach not only reduces Hausdorff95 (HD95) by 33.9% and Average Surface Distance (ASD) by 42.1% compared with the state-of-the-art method, but it also achieves excellent results on the minute quantity of datasets, which greatly improves the feasibility of automatic root canal therapy evaluation by medical image computing.

This academic paper presents a novel method for resource allocation in multiple input, multiple output (MIMO) radar systems with non-coherent localization of multiple targets. The key contribution of this work is to develop an efficient algorithm that determines optimal resource allocation strategies for target tracking and detection tasks by considering both spatial and temporal correlations among targets. Our proposed approach utilizes Bayesian optimization and machine learning techniques to efficiently search through the large solution space and extract critical features from data samples from the MIMO radar system using Gaussian process regression models, which are trained on simulated or real-world data samples to make use of maximum performance in non-coherency scenarios. As we demonstrate in our experimental results, these methods allow us to optimize resource allocation while minimizing computational complexity and improving precision in detection and tracking of multiple targets in non-cluttered environments.

This academic paper explores the use of mask-based data augmentation techniques for improving the performance of semi-supervised semantic segmentation models. By generating synthetic training data through mask-based augmentation, the model is able to learn more robust features and achieve better segmentation results on limited labeled data. The paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of various mask-based augmentation strategies and demonstrates their effectiveness in improving the accuracy and robustness of the semantic segmentation model. Overall, the proposed approach provides a simple yet effective way to enhance the performance of semi-supervised semantic segmentation models, especially in scenarios with limited labeled data.

This academic paper presents innovative approach to synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) image segmentation using iterative, deep, and unsupervised learning technique. The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to segment SAS images into their constituent parts, without need for manual annotation or supervised training. The approach is based on an iterative process that refines the segmentation results at each iteration, leading to improved accuracy and robustness. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive experiments on real-world SAS datasets, showing significant improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods. Overall, this paper provides promising solution for SAS image segmentation that is both efficient and accurate, paving the way for further advancements in underwater image analysis.

Abstract: Speech has long been argued to be capable of three main semantic functions, which can be characterized by their fundamental frequency and their varying magnitude over time. This study quantifies, in terms of lexical density and phonological distances among languages, which of these three functions of speech is predominating in a given language when changes caused by natural language texts within a given population are being considered. We consider these changes as the outcome of the difference in reading style, or even simply the differences in the readability standards used in different cultures. The result is that at any given scale, there is no general trend in the lexical density of languages, except for language change, especially in the early stages. The distribution of overall lexicality is quite similar on different dimensions. But linguistic properties such as the number of words per word unit, the pitch accent patterns and vowel forms in English, are strongly correlated. Hence, the apparent meaning of these features is not only a problem of measurement, but an artifact of our approach, which also allows us to study complex interactions among them.

In this work, we address the difficult task of few-shot segmentation. Recent few-shot segmentation methods usually employ the information of support images as guidance for query image segmentation. While some works intend to establish cross-reference between support and query images, their extraction of query data mostly depends on the support images. We here intend to extract the info from the database itself independently to benefit the few-shot segmentation task. To this end, we first propose a prior extractor to learn the query information from the unlabeled images with our proposed global-local contrastive learning. Then, we extract a set of predetermined priors through this previous extractor. With the obtained priors, we produce the prior region maps for query images, which locate the objects, as guidance to perform cross interaction with support features. In such a manner, the extraction of query data is detached from the help branch, avoiding the limitation by support, and can provide more useful query clues to obtain greater communication. With bells and bells, the proposed method creates new state-of-the-art performance for the few-shot segmentation task on PASCAL-5$^{i}$ and COCO datasets.

Large-scale image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision systems. In this work, we present a novel approach to perform image partitioning using distributed clustering algorithms such as K-means and hierarchical clustering. Our method aims at addressing the problems of large data processing by splitting the image into smaller subimages that can be processed separately and then using their results to derive a final output. We therefore propose an adaptive approach to rearrange the partitions of large clusters with minimal communication overhead, which reduces efficiency. The algorithm converges better than traditional methods by using MPI (Message Passing Interface) for parallel communication between nodes. Results show that our proposed technique outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches, gaining comparable reliability with reduced computational time and communicative cost.

3D Convolution Neural Systems (CNNs) have been extensively used to 3D scene understanding, such as video analysis and volumetric picture recognition. Moreover, 3D networks can readily lead to over-parameterization which reduces expensive computational cost. In this paper, we propose Channel-wise Automatic KErnel Shrinking (CAKES), to provide optimal 3D learning by shrinking standard 3D convolutions into a set of economic operations e.g., 1D, 2D convolutions. Like previous technologies, CAKES performs channel-wise kernel shrinkage, which enjoys the following advantages: 1) allowing operations implemented in each layer to be heterogeneous, so that they can extract diverse and complementary information to benefit the learning process; and 2) providing for an efficient and flexible replacement design, which can be generalized to both spatial-temporal and volumetric databases. Further, we propose a new search space based on CAKES, so that the replacement topology can be determined automatically for simplifying 3D networks. CAKES displays comparable efficiency to other protocols with comparable model size, and it often achieves superior efficiency to state-of-the-art with much smaller parameters and computational costs on tasks including 3D medical imaging segmentation and video action recognition. Codes and models are accessible at http://github.com/yucornetto/CAKES

The reliability of Deep Learning systems depends on their accuracy but also on their robustness against adversarial perturbations to the input data. Several attacks and defences have been proposed to improve the performance of Deep Neural Networks under the presence of adversarial noise in the natural image domain. However, robustness in computer-aided diagnosis for volumetric data has only been explored for specific tasks and with limited attacks. We propose a new framework to assess the robustness of general medical image segmentation systems. Our contributions are two-fold: (i) we propose a new benchmark to evaluate robustness in the context of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) by extending the recent AutoAttack natural image classification framework to the domain of volumetric data segmentation, and (ii) we present a novel lattice architecture for RObust Generic medical image segmentation (ROG). Our results show that ROG is capable of generalising across different tasks of the MSD and largely surpasses the state-of-the-art under sophisticated adversarial attacks.

One issue limiting the adaption of large-scale multi-region segmentation is the sometimes prohibitive memory requirements. This is especially troubling considering advances in massively parallel computing and commercial graphics processing units because of their already limited memory compared to the current random access memory used in more traditional computation. To address this issue in the field of continuous max-flow segmentation, we have developed a pseudo-flow framework using the theory of Bregman proximal projections and entropic distances which implicitly represents flow variables between labels and designated source and sink nodes. This reduces the memory requirements for max-flow segmentation by approximately 20 for Potts models and approximately 30 for hierarchical max-flow (HMF) and directed acyclic graph max-flow (DAGMF) models. This represents a great improvement in the state-of-the-art in max-flow segmentation, allowing for much larger problems to be addressed and accelerated using commercially available graphics processing hardware.

This paper aims to develop a novel unsupervised technique for semantic image segmentation, using two of the most powerful methods of style synthesis and vision: a new technique for unsupervised learning of images using GANs, and a method for understanding images based on a large dataset. We use pre-trained SegGANs and Clip, two highly specialized, narrowly focused, image-style generative models. Testing shows that our method achieves similar performance to that of supervised learning algorithms, while reducing the computational complexity and time required for training, which makes it a more practical solution for applications in the field of medical image diagnosis and self-driving vehicles.

This academic paper presents a novel approach for high-resolution segmentation of tooth root fuzzy edges based on polynomial curve fitting with landmark detection. The proposed method utilizes landmark detection to identify key points on the tooth root image, which are then fitted with a polynomial curve to accurately segment the tooth root fuzzy edge. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through experimental results, which show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The paper concludes that the proposed method is a promising approach for high-resolution segmentation of tooth root fuzzy edges and has potential applications in dental imaging and analysis.

Salient object detection (SOD) is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves identifying and segmenting the most visually distinct or interesting objects or regions in an image. While traditional SOD methods rely on bottom-up or top-down approaches, this paper proposes a novel discriminative regional feature integration approach. Our method combines the strengths of both bottom-up and top-down methods, leveraging the rich semantic information in the image. We first introduce a novel regional feature extraction method that captures the spatial and spectral information of the image. The regional features are then integrated using a discriminative manner, which allows the model to learn the importance of each feature for salient object detection. This is achieved through a novel spatial pyramid pooling module that effectively fuses the regional features at multiple scales. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, including ECSSD, HKU-IS, and THUR15K. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art SOD methods, including bottom-up and top-down approaches. Specifically, our method achieves a significant improvement in terms of mean absolute error (MAE) and structural similarity index (SSIM). The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows: 1. We propose a novel discriminative regional feature integration approach for salient object detection, which combines the strengths of bottom-up and top-down methods. 2. We introduce a regional feature extraction method that captures the spatial and spectral information of the image. 3. We design a novel spatial pyramid pooling module that effectively fuses the regional features at multiple scales. 4. Our approach outperforms state-of-the-art SOD methods on several benchmark datasets. Overall, this paper presents a significant advancement in salient object detection research, providing a new perspective on how to integrate regional features in a discriminative manner. The proposed method has important implications for a wide range of applications, including image and video analysis, object recognition, and scene understanding.

Abstract: Medical image segmentation is a critical step towards extracting valuable information from medical images, enabling improved diagnosis and treatment. While much progress has been made in this area, current methods remain vulnerable to various challenges such as poor illumination, contrast variation, and anatomical complexity. This work presents a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art deep learning techniques for general medical image segmentation, focusing on their strengths and weaknesses. We discuss hybrid approaches that combine multiple model architectures to improve performance across diverse imaging modalities and pathologies. Finally, we explore future research directions aimed at enhancing the robustness and generalizability of these models, including transfer learning, multi-task learning, and active learning strategies. Overall, this work provides insights into the current landscape of general medical image segmentation and identifies promising avenues for addressing remaining challenges.

In this paper, we propose a novel method to enforce perceptual consistency in generative adversarial networks (GANs). We use the normalized Laplacian pyramid distance to measure the dissimilarity between images generated from different GAN models. Specifically, we use two types of Laplacian pyramids: the global one that captures features at all scales and the local one that focuses on small patches or regions of interest. The normalized Laplacian pyramid distance is calculated using an iterative optimization algorithm that minimizes the squared difference between the feature vectors of the input and output images. Our experimental results show that our proposed method effectively enforces perceptual consistency across different GAN architectures and produces visually more realistic images compared to existing methods.

The GraphBLAS standard (graphblas.org) is being developed to make the potential of graph-algorithms matrix-based to the largest possible audience. Mathematically, GraphBLAS provides a core set of graph-algorithms that are based on matrices and that are used to implement many graph-algorithms in various languages. In this paper, we will explain the mathema-tics of GraphBLAS. Graphs are used to represent connections between nodes through the edges connecting them. Matrices can represent a wide range of graphs using adjacency or incidence matrices. Adjacency matrices are often easier to analyze; incidence matrices are often better for representing data. Fortunately, these two things are easy to combine by multiplication. A key feature of the mathematics of matrices is that a very small number of matrix operations can be used to manage a very wide range of graphs. This combinability of small operations is the basis of GraphBLAS. A standard like GraphBLAS can only be successful if it is efficient. Measurements of the performance of GraphBLAS implementations indicate that the overhead is small.

The development of artificial intelligance (AI) has revolutionized various industries, including healthcare. With its potential to improve medical imaging accuracy and speed, AI is increasingly being integrated into clinical workflows for image analysis and interpretation. However, concerns arise about the reliability and trustworthiness of AI systems in this setting. In this paper, we outline guiding principles for building trustworthy AI in future medical imaging using concensus recommendations from a group of experts in the field. Our framework considers multiple dimensions such as data quality, model transparency, human oversight, ethical implications, and patient privacy. We also propose guidelines on how to measure and evaluate AI performance, validate models on new datasets, and incorporate knowledge exchange between humans and machines. These recommendations provide practical insights that can help ensure the responsible use of AI technologies with high stakes, ultimately leading to better outcomes for patients and improving healthcare delivery.

This paper presents a novel approach for high-resolution segmentation of tooth root fuzzy edges based on polynomial curve fitting with landmark detection. The proposed method aims to accurately separate the tooth roots from the surrounding dental tissues in digital dental images. Existing methods for tooth root segmentation are often limited by their reliance on hand-crafted features, low accuracy, and high computational complexity. In contrast, our approach leverages the power of polynomial curve fitting to accurately model the fuzzy edges of tooth roots and detect landmarks that define the boundary between the tooth roots and the surrounding tissues. The proposed method consists of three stages: 7) preprocessing, 2) polynomial curve fitting, and 1) landmark detection. In the preprocessing stage, the input image is filtered to enhance the contrast and remove noise. In the polynomial curve fitting stage, a cubic polynomial curve is fitted to the fuzzy edge of the tooth root using a non-linear least squares optimization algorithm. The curve is then used to separate the tooth root from the surrounding tissues. Finally, landmarks are detected by identifying the points on the curve that correspond to the maximum gradient values. The proposed method was evaluated on a dataset of 20 digital dental images using a leave-one-out cross-validation scheme. The results show that our method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. The mean absolute error was found to be 0.15 mm, and the processing time was less than 67 seconds per image. The proposed method has important implications for dental image analysis and related applications such as orthodontic treatment planning, dental implant planning, and oral disease diagnosis. With its high accuracy, efficiency, and robustness, the method has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of dental procedures and contribute to better patient outcomes.

## Abstract The main challenges in computer assisted diagnosis (CAD) systems are accurate and explainable diagnostic results that can augment medical decisions beyond traditional visual interpretation methods. To address these needs, we have developed a novel machine learning approach based on physics first principles to infer explanatory physical structures that underlie cardiovascular diseases directly from patient-specific imaging data. Our model has two parts: the forward solver produces numerical solutions of the blood flow equations assuming known cardiac structure; and deep neural nets compute best approximations or surrogates to this solution using information derived only from noncontrast magnetic resonance images. Using cardiovascular data collected over 5 years, our initial experiments show compelling evidence that both training and inference time is greatly reduced compared to end-to-end supervised approaches. This allows us to build models much larger than what would be practical otherwise. In addition preliminary experimental investigations found higher accuracy when trained with simulated data vs ground truth. We believe better understanding of complex hemodynamic behaviors through such interpretable models may lead to discovery of new underlying risk factors that help patients and doctors better understand their disease state for improved therapeutic decision making.

While improving prediction accuracy has been the focus of machine learning in recent years, this alone does not suffice for reliable decision-making. Deploying learning systems in consequential settings also requires calibrating and communicating the uncertainty of predictions. To convey instance-wise uncertainty for prediction tasks, we show how to generate set-valued predictions from a black-box predictor that control the expected loss on future test points at a user-specified level. Our approach provides explicit finite-sample guarantees for any dataset by using a holdout set to calibrate the size of the prediction sets. This framework enables simple, distribution-free, rigorous error control for many tasks, and we demonstrate it in five large-scale machine learning problems: (1) classification problems where some mistakes are more costly than others; (2) multi-label classification, where each observation has multiple associated labels; (3) classification problems where the labels have a hierarchical structure; (4) image segmentation, where we wish to predict a set of pixels containing an object of interest; and (5) protein structure prediction. Lastly, we discuss extensions to uncertainty quantification for ranking, metric learning and distributionally robust learning.

In this paper, we investigate the concept of privacy amplification, which refers to the idea That An individual's private information can be protected by amplifying the noise in their data without sacrificing the accuracy of statistical analyses performed On that data. We show that non-signaling privacy amplification, a specific type of privacy amplification that does not rely on any assumptions about the distribution of the private information, is impossible in the presence of a non-trivial adversary. We demonstrate that any attempt to amplify privacy without signaling the private information will necessarily result in a trade-off between privacy and accuracy, and that it Is impossible to achieve both simultaneously. Specifically, we prove that any privacy amplification Method that does not signal the private information must either significantly degrade the accuracy of statistical analyses or else reveal information about the private data. Our results have important Implications for the design of privacy-preserving data Analysis systems. In particular, they suggest that it May be necessary to reconsider the assumption that privacy can be protected without sacrificing accuracy, and to explore alternative approaches that explicitly take into account the potential risks and trade-offs involved in privacy-preserving data analysis. Overall, our paper highlights the challenges and limitations of privacy amplification, and provides a new perspective on the privacy-accuracy trade-off in data analysis. Our findings Have important implications for policymakers, Researchers, and practitioners working in the field of privacy-preserving data analysis, and suggest that a more nuanced understanding of the privacy-accuracy trade-off is necessary in order to Develop effective and practical privacy-preserving Data analysis systems.

We investigate optimum shapes and locations of defects in two-dimensional lattices made of lossy material to create high quality mesoscopic optical resonances, referred to as cavity QED cells or atoms. Using simple variational calculations we show that circular shaped cells with radius slightly smaller than lattice constant are extremely robust against variation of cell parameters. We also demonstrate that there exist positions on honeycomb lattice such that when the cell contains only one atom inside it exhibits nearly ideal transmission spectrum (transparency). Moreover our approach yields much sharper results concerning dependence of spectral properties of cell on its frequency location compared to standard model of single atom embedded into an infinite array. Finally we analyze possibility that several atomic emitters can be coupled using our kind of optical cavities without strong interaction between them (avoiding problem known as superradiance). This could lead to experimental demonstration of entangled states of light.

Artificial intelligence (AI), and particularly machine learning, has become increasingly prevalent within healthcare as diagnostic support technology known as artificial intelligence medical systems, with applications spanning multiple areas including radiology and pathology imaging data interpretation but also genomics to facilitate precision medicine efforts. In response to this rapid innovation dynamic, we seek to help ensure that AI within all contexts of health care are trustworthy through lens of human-machine collaboration. Toward these ends, experts representing a diversity of disciplines engaged across government agencies, academic institutions, industry leaders, and patient advocacy group representatives gathered at international workshop entitled FUTURE-AI. A major goal was to elucidate how best practices could be developed toward achieving trustworthiness of AI systems utilized throughout radiological clinical practice workflows from pre-training inputs through validation methodologies to final deployment and ongoing use assessment frameworks. More specifically, during sessions over five days participants identified key principles pertinent to designing machine intelligence technologies in conjunction with humans on which future guidance documents can be built. Topics included definitions of terms such as explainability, fairness and bias, transparency and accessibility; ethical considerations around human factors involved in the design of intelligent machines especially when applied clinically; and approaches to training, testing, validating and deploying models in realistic clinical environments for diverse patient populations. Participants also assessed gaps in existing AI standards and made suggestions regarding necessary improvements or updates currently lacking in order to promote future safe system development and implementation, ultimately leading to recommendations for moving forward along established guidelines. Through this consensus process, we hope to inform best practices for using advanced computer science analytics towards helping physicians deliver optimal patient outcomes.

Training deep networks with limited labeled data while achieving a strong generalization ability is key in the quest to reduce human annotation efforts. This is the goal of semi-supervised learning, which exploits more widely available unlabeled data to complement small labeled data sets. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for discriminative pixel-level tasks using a generative model of both images and labels. Concretely, we learn a generative adversarial network that captures the joint image-label distribution and is trained efficiently using a large set of unlabeled images supplemented with only few labeled ones. We build our architecture on top of StyleGAN2, augmented with a label synthesis branch. Image labeling at test time is achieved by first embedding the target image into the joint latent space via an encoder network and test-time optimization, and then generating the label from the inferred embedding. We evaluate our approach in two important domains: medical image segmentation and part-based face segmentation. We demonstrate strong in-domain performance compared to several baselines, and are the first to showcase extreme out-of-domain generalization, such as transferring from CT to MRI in medical imaging, and photographs of real faces to paintings, sculptures, and even cartoons and animal faces. This paper describes a novel approach to semantic segmentation, based on variational reaction-diffusion systems. Our method uses the ability of such systems to efficiently model complex physical processes, such as heat diffusion and fluid dynamics, to model the propagation of information across an image. By adapting the classical equation of Fisher from population dynamics, we create a new framework which gives efficient and accurate semantic segmentation. We show that our method outperforms the state of the art in both accuracy and speed. A detailed analysis of the effect of different parameters on the performance of the proposed method gives a clear insight into the workings of the algorithm. Our main contributions can be summarized as follows. We propose a novel method of semantic segmentation, based on variational reaction-diffusion systems. We adapt the equation of Fisher from population dynamics to semantic segmentation. We show that the proposed method is accurate and efficient on several test data sets.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of healthcare, enabling the accurate identification and extraction of specific anatomical structures from medical images. However, the complexity and variability of medical images make this task challenging. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for robust and generalised medical image segmentation. Our framework utilises a combination of deep learning techniques and domain-specific knowledge to improve the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation process. We also introduce a novel data augmentation technique to enhance the generalisation ability of the model. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on various medical image datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Overall, our work contributes to the development of a more reliable and versatile tool for medical image segmentation.

A posteriori error estimates are constructed for the three-field variational formulation of the Biot problem involving the displacements, the total pressure and the fluid pressure. The discretization under focus is the H 1 (O) -conforming Taylor-Hood finite element combination, consisting of polynomial degrees k 1 for the displacements and the fluid pressure and k for the total pressure. An a posteriori error estimator is derived on the basis of H (div) -conforming reconstructions of the stress and flux approximations. The symmetry of the reconstructed stress is allowed to be satisfied only weakly. The reconstructions can be performed locally on a set of vertex patches and lead to a guaranteed upper bound for the error with a constant that depends only on local constants associated with the patches and thus on the shape regularity of the triangulation. Particular emphasis is given to nearly incompressible materials and the error estimates hold uniformly in the incompressible limit. Numerical results on the L-shaped domain confirm the theory and the suitable use of the error estimator in adaptive strategies.

Cardiac MR image segmentation is a key technique in analysis of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging data. This process involves identifying and separating specific structures within the heart, such as myocardium, endomyocardium, epicardium, left ventricle, right ventricle, and atria, from surrounding background tissue. In recent years, various techniques have been developed to perform this task, including region growing, thresholding, edges detection, active contour modeling, deformable models, and deep learning-based approaches. This paper provides overview of these cardiac MR image segmentation techniques, discussing their strengths and weaknesses, and highlighting current trends and challenges. The paper also discusses the role of manual human intervention versus automated computer-aided detection methods in achieving accurate results. Additionally, potential applications of semantic segmentation techniques in assisting clinical decision making are explored. Overall, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of cardiac MR image segmentation techniques, with practical implications for researchers and clinicians alike.

In this research article, we present novel approach to detect mammography edges using hybrid soft computing methods. We first conducted an extensive literature review of different edge detection techniques in mammography and found that many traditional methods struggle with identifying subtle changes in tissue density due to their reliance on binary classification. Our proposed method utilizes fuzzy logic controllers (FLC) to generate gradient map based on gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM). The gradient map is then overlaid onto the original image using adaptive thresholding. Furthermore, we introduce wavelet transform (WT) into our edge detection framework by utilizing its multiscale nature to filter out noise while preserving significant details at multiple resolution levels. We evaluated our proposed method on large dataset of digital breast tomosynthesis images and achieved superior results compared to traditional edge detection algorithms. Our findings demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating soft computing methods such as FLC and WT in detecting subtle variations in tissue density, thereby increasing the accuracy of mammographic edge detection.

End-to-End Deep Convolutional Active Contours for Image Segmentation: A novel approach that involves training deep neural networks as active contour models for image segmentation is presented. The proposed architecture integrates an encoder-decoder network structure with the active learning framework to optimize the training process of salient object detection in dynamic scenes. Through this technique, we leverage the advantages of both traditional machine learning and computer vision techniques for improved model generalization and accuracy. Our experiments show significant improvement in the performance for detecting semantically complex objects with high precision rates and reduced computational costs compared to state-of-the-art methods. Overall, our work demonstrates a promising path towards practical end-to-end convolutional active learning for image segmentation on real-world applications.

> This research addresses three common scenarios in the use of deep neural networks (DNN) to train medical image segmentation models, namely using large data and noisy labels. Such conditions can lead to DNN suffering during model optimization and generalization problems. We propose a quick and simple solution to these issues, which are interrelated. Our proposed approach consists of analyzing simulation values in tandem with training data augmentations such that our resulting pipeline provides a bigger regularizer than other methods typically used by practitioners. Experimental findings demonstrate efficiency increases over standard solutions when both small training datasets and missing or incomplete labels occur concurrently.
