This study introduces a comprehensive multi-modal interaction approach for referring image segmentation, which utilizes both natural language and visual cues to accurately segment objects in images. The proposed method employs state-of-the-art deep learning models that effectively combine various modalities such as text descriptions, object localization maps, attention mechanisms, and feature embeddings. Extensive experimental evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our model over existing baselines on three benchmark datasets, highlighting its potential applications in visual question answering,image captioning,and other related tasks. Overall, this work provides valuable insights into designing effective multimodal fusion strategies tailoredforreferring image segmentation problems.

Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) image segmentation based on iterative, deep, and unsupervised learning techniques. SAS imageing is widely used in underwater exploration and surveillance, but its low-quality images pose significant challenges for accurate target detection and segmentation. Existing methods rely heavily on manual annotation and domain-specific feature extraction, which are time-consuming, tedious, and suboptimal. To address these limitations, we propose an iterative, deep, and unsupervised method that leverages recent advances in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and clustreing algorithms. Our approach consists of two main stages: (1) preliminary feature extraction using a CNN; and (2) iterative clustreing and refinement enabled by a self-organising map (SOM). The CNN extracts high-level features from the input SAS images, while the SOM grouping fosters spatial coherence and facilitates the formation of meaningful clustres. An iterative mechanism integrates the CNN and SOM outputs, allowing the algorithm to adaptively refine its segmentations as more data becomes available. Our exhaustive experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method over traditional approaches, achieving an average precision increase of 15% and a mean IoU improvement of 0.3. Additionally, we provide thorough analyses of parametre sensitivity and performance consistency across different scenarios, offering insights into the strengths and limitations of deep, unsupervised SAS image segmentation. The contributions of this work can be summarised as follows: * Novel use of CNNs and SOMs for joint feature extraction and clustre identification in SAS image segmentation * Introduction of an iterative mechanism to improve segmentation accuracy through active learning * Comprehensive evaluation and analysis of performance metrics to establish reliability and robustness * Enhanced applicability to diverse underwater environments thanks to the lack of dependence on manually labelled data or domain-specific heuristics The proposed method has far-reaching implications for improving the efficiency and effect

The global Fukaya category is a framework for studying symplectic topology which was introduced by Gromov and Witten in their seminal paper. This category contains rich information about symplectic knots, surfaces, and more general geometrical objects, including smooth maps. In recent years, it has undergone significant expansion due to various developments in different areas of mathematics such as differential geometry, complex analysis, and representation theory. In this review article, we survey some aspects of the global Fukaya category II and its associated theories. Specifically, we focus on its application to classical singular connections on manifolds and provide overview of obstructions in terms of quantum theory. We also discuss applications in other areas such as geometric Langlands programs and Mori-Ribet's theorem for threefolds with singularities. Lastly, we mention some open problems and future directions for research. Overall, our aim is to highlight the importance and flexibility of this conceptual scheme in connecting disparate fields within mathematics and physics.

The reliability of Deep Learning systems depends on their accuracy but also on their robustness against adversarial perturbations to the input data. Several attacks and defenses have been proposed to improve the performance of Deep Neural Networks under the presence of adversarial noise in the natural image domain. However, robustness in computer-aided diagnosis for volumetric data has only been explored for specific tasks and with limited attacks. We propose a new framework to assess the robustness of general medical image segmentation systems. Our contributions are two-fold: (i) we propose a new benchmark to evaluate robustness in the context of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) by extending the recent AutoAttack natural image classification framework to the domain of volumetric data segmentation, and (ii) we present a novel lattice architecture for RObust Generic medical image segmentation (ROG). Our results show that ROG is capable of generalizing across different tasks of the MSD and largely surpasses the state-of-the-art under sophisticated adversarial attacks.

This study aimed to develop a robust general medical image segmentation algorithm. A comprehensive review of existing techniques was conducted, and an innovative approach combining deep learning with traditional machine learning methods was proposed. The effectiveness of the method was demonstrated through extensive experiments on multiple datasets covering various anatomical structures and imaging modalities. Results showed that the proposed methodology significantly improved segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the art models, making it a promising tool for clinicians and researchers in the field of medical imaging.

Increasingly, many argue that elementary statistics should be a mandatory subject in the high school curriculum. I agree with this wholeheartedly, as the discipline has become central to civic and economic literacy in the 21st century. But to argue, as some have, that this should replace the traditional "algebra to calculus" high school math sequence makes about as much sense to me as arguing that history should replace English. While the two undoubtedly share some skills and mechanics, they are fundamentally different disciplines with fundamentally different roles in the curriculum, and both are necessary for a complete education. Although the underlying mechanics of statistics are undoubtedly mathematical, increasingly it is becoming recognized as a discipline in its own right, with its own methodology and best practices distinct from those of pure mathematics, and the structure of high school should reflect this divergence. At the high school level, the focus of statistics pedagogy should be on core concepts, the appropriate use of technology, and interpretation you are teaching a student to turn data into an accurate, precise probablistic statement, and to have an intuitive understanding of the probability concepts underlying the meaning of that statement. These are important skills, but they aren't really mathematical skills in the traditional sense; you are reasoning in a different mode. In a well-taught algebra, geometry, or calculus class, by contrast, students learn to reason deductively rather than inductively, learn the theory underlying core mathematical notions such as function and equivalence, solve non-routine problems, and use mathematics of all types to analyze real-world phenomena. None of these skills except arguably the last play any role in an elementary statistics curriculum. You can argue that a deep facility with "abstract" math has little importance in the "real world," but increasingly the 21st century economy does reward individuals who have a high capacity for abstraction and problem-solving, even if you are never directly using specific skills (the classic "when will I ever need the quadratic formula in real life" bugbear). Finally, learning these mathematical concepts is a necessary prerequisite for any further study in STEM fields, which statistics training will not replace. Thus, BOTH statistics and math, as separate disciplines, should have a role in the high school curriculum. Two centuries ago, it was established that the average human body temperature was 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit, or 37 degrees Celsius. Scientists have noticed a drop in average body temperature in recent years and theorized it's because of climate change. Recent studies involving over 500 subjects found an average person's core temperature dropped by half-a-degree from 2012 to 2017 - enough for many people noticing their hands are less warm than they used to be when exercising outdoors. (The study also concluded there is no significant link between decreased activity levels and low temperatures.) If you hadn't already heard about this research, here are five reasons your body might actually feel colder than ever. One way to figure if you're suffering through sub-zero weather is feeling tired all day long without having gotten much sleep at night before heading outside into the elements. If you're always thinking something could go wrong with your energy level during harsh winter months but end up sleeping fine every subsequent summer, chances are you don't need more caffeine to get going after dark anymore (and now that's entirely believable).

We study the lexicographically least infinite $a/b$-power-free word on the alphabet of non-negative integers. Frequently this word is a fixed point of a uniform morphism, or closely related to one. For example, the lexicographically least $7/4$-power-free word is a fixed point of a $50847$-uniform morphism. We identify the structure of the lexicographically least $a/b$-power-free word for three infinite families of rationals $a/b$ as well many "sporadic" rationals that do not seem to belong to general families. To accomplish this, we develop an automated procedure for proving $a/b$-power-freeness for morphisms of a certain form, both for explicit and symbolic rational numbers $a/b$. Finally, we establish a connection to words on a finite alphabet. Namely, the lexicographically least $27/23$-power-free word is in fact a word on the finite alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, and its sequence of letters is $353$-automatic.

In this paper, we present EdgeFlow, a novel approach to interactive segmentation that leverages the concept of edge-guided flow to achieve practical and efficient segmentation of images. Interactive segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves allowing a user to interact with an image to indicate the regions of interest. However, existing methods for interactive segmentation are often limited by their reliance on iterative user input, which can be time-consuming and may not accurately capture the user's intended segmentation. EdgeFlow addresses these limitations by introducing a new approach that combines the efficiency of edge-guided segmentation with the practicality of interactive segmentation. Our approach uses a novel edge-guided flow algorithm that propagates user input along the edges of an image, allowing for fast and accurate segmentation of complex images. We demonstrate the effectiveness of EdgeFlow through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets, showing that it outperforms state-of-the-art interactive segmentation methods in terms of both efficiency and accuracy. In addition, we explore the versatility of EdgeFlow by applying it to a variety of applications, including object segmentation, medical image segmentation, and video segmentation. Our results show that EdgeFlow can handle a wide range of scenarios, from simple object segmentation to complex medical image segmentation, and can accurately segment objects in real-time. Overall, EdgeFlow represents a significant advancement in the field of interactive segmentation, providing a practical and efficient approach that can be used in a variety of applications. Its ability to accurately segment images with minimal user input makes it an ideal tool for a wide range of users, from researchers to practitioners.

Music recommender systems (MRS) have experienced a boom in recent years, thanks to the emergence and success of online streaming services, which nowadays make available almost all music in the world at the user's fingertip. While today's MRS considerably help users to find interesting music in these huge catalogs, MRS research is still facing substantial challenges. In particular when it comes to build, incorporate, and evaluate recommendation strategies that integrate information beyond simple user-item interactions or content-based descriptors, but dig deep into the very essence of listener needs, preferences, and intentions, MRS research becomes a big endeavor and related publications quite sparse. The purpose of this trends and survey article is twofold. We first identify and shed light on what we believe are the most pressing challenges MRS research is facing, from both academic and industry perspectives. We review the state of the art towards solving these challenges and discuss its limitations. Second, we detail possible future directions and visions we contemplate for the further evolution of the field. The article should therefore serve two purposes: giving the interested reader an overview of current challenges in MRS research and providing guidance for young researchers by identifying interesting, yet under-researched, directions in the field.

Since its renaissance, deep learning has been widely used in various medical imaging tasks and has achieved remarkable success in many medical imaging applications, thereby propelling us into the so-called artificial intelligence (AI) era. It is known that the success of AI is mostly attributed to the availability of big data with annotations for a single task and the advances in high performance computing. However, medical imaging presents unique challenges that confront deep learning approaches. In this survey paper, we first highlight both clinical needs and technical challenges in medical imaging and describe how emerging trends in deep learning are addressing these issues. We cover the topics of network architecture, sparse and noisy labels, federating learning, interpretability, uncertainty quantification, etc. Then, we present several case studies that are commonly found in clinical practice, including digital pathology and chest, brain, cardiovascular, and abdominal imaging. Rather than presenting an exhaustive literature survey, we instead describe some prominent research highlights related to these case study applications. We conclude with a discussion and presentation of promising future directions.

The Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation is a well-known nonlinear partial differential equation that describes the propagation of waves in shallow water. In this paper, we study the isospectral deformation of the KdV equation, which is a technique used to transform the original equation into a new equation with the same spectrum. We show that this technique can be used to create complex breathers, which are solutions to the KdV equation that exhibit oscillatory behavior in both space and time. We also show that the complex breathers can be obtained by combining free particle solutions to the KdV equation. Our results provide a new insight into the behavior of complex breathers and have potential applications in fields such as physics, engineering, and computer science.

She heard the door open, the noise of the closet's door being slammed. Mom's mouth opened. No words, but she mouthed, "Bitsy, what are you doing?" Bitsy was startled. She could not say a word. "Bitsy, what are you doing?" Mom's eyes showed concern. Bitsy's eyes welled with tears. No answer, her face betrayed her fear. Mother reached out, slowly removed the blanket from her daughter, cradled her in her arms. Bitsy's face buried in her mother's bosom. "Oh, my Bitsy, I am so sorry."

In recent years, there has been a surge in research on political collective action using data from Twitter. However, many studies have faced criticism for biases embedded in their methods and data. This paper presents a critical review of existing literature on this topic, with a focus on identifying these potential biases and evaluating their impact on the results. We find that several methods commonly used in the field suffer from selection bias, which can lead to inaccurate conclusions about collective behavior. Additionally, we argue that Twitter itself may be prone to network effects that amplify certain voices or perspectives over others, potentially leading to an echo chamber effect. Our findings highlight the need for researchers to carefully consider their study designs and data sources when studying political collective action on social media platforms like Twitter. Ultimately, addressing these biases is crucial for developing reliable insights into how these communities function and potentially improving strategies for mobilizing them towards specific goals.

Incorporating a human-in-the-loop system when deploying automated decision support is critical in healthcare contexts to create trust, as well as provide reliable performance on a patient-to-patient basis. Deep learning methods while having high performance, do not allow for this patient-centered approach due to the lack of uncertainty representation. Thus, we present a framework of uncertainty representation evaluated for medical image segmentation, using MCU-Net which combines a U-Net with Monte Carlo Dropout, evaluated with four different uncertainty metrics. The framework augments this by adding a human-in-the-loop aspect based on an uncertainty threshold for automated referral of uncertain cases to a medical professional. We demonstrate that MCU-Net combined with epistemic uncertainty and an uncertainty threshold tuned for this application maximizes automated performance on an individual patient level, yet refers truly uncertain cases. This is a step towards uncertainty representations when deploying machine learning based decision support in healthcare settings.

Fast barcode retrieval is a crucial component in consensus contouring, which aims to perform automated segmentation on medical images. However, this process can be time-consuming if done manually, especially when dealing with complex objects or multiple variants of the same object. To overcome these challenges, researchers have proposed various techniques that utilize machine learning and computer vision approaches to automatically retrieve barcodes from medical images. These methods incorporate feature extraction, classification, clustering, and other algorithms to accurately identify and group similar barcodes, thereby reducing manual intervention and speeding up the process. Some studies also explore the use of deep learning models such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to streamline the barcode identification process by training on large datasets with labeled data. In terms of accuracy, several fast barcode retrieval methods have been tested using ground truth annotations provided by human experts. Results have shown promising improvements over basic techniques, particularly regarding specificity, recall, precision, and F1 score metrics. The ability to automate barcode retrieval has not only helped increase efficiency but also allowed researchers to analyze larger datasets more comprehensively and effectively evaluate different image processing strategies. Overall, the field of fast barcode retrieval offers great potential in advancing automated console contouring and improving the overall quality of disease diagnosis and treatment.

The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is set to launch on Halloween this year, after decades of careful planning and development. It will travel from Earth to a gravitational eddy in space that causes the telescope's light to accelerate like a rocket. There are four parts to JWST: the optical telescope; the imaging spectrograph, also known as the "bunker"; the infrared mirror; and the high-energy ultraviolet detector. The whole mission was first proposed by NASA in 1990 and has been kept secret for more than 30 years due to security concerns. Now, some staffers at Goddard say they don't know why it's taking so long now. "It seems pretty clear, even during its design phase, what you need onboard. But we've never had something exactly work out," said William Greaves, who oversees the project at Goddard's Space Flight Facility in Greenbelt, Maryland. "So now with all these different pieces coming together, frankly I'm not sure why they're still going through this process." At the moment everything looks good but NASA is still working to figure out the exact details of the instruments' performance: how much light they can see, where it should fall on the spectrum and whether anything will be missed because of noise. To speed up the analysis, engineers have increased the number of active instruments on board - which increases the chances that a single instrument won't operate properly or gather data as expected if there's an interruption in power supply during flight. Goddard expects final engineering designs will be ready within five months. Once designed, NASA then needs approval from Congress before construction begins in 2018. That could take several years longer.

In this paper, we present a novel approach for generating complex breathers in the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation through isospectral deformation of the free particle system. By exploiting the connection between the KdV equation and the spectral problem of the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation, we show that the free particle can be used as a seed solution to generate a wide range of complex breathers with arbitrary amplitude and velocity. Using the isospectral deformation method, we demonstrate that the free particle solution can be deformed into a family of nonlinear breathers with distinct dynamical behaviors, including periodic, quasi-periodic, and chaotic motion. We show that these breathers exhibit a rich variety of structures, including single-layer, multi-layer, and vortex-like patterns, and that they can be controlled by adjusting the parameters of the deformation. Our results provide a new and efficient way to generate complex breathers in the KdV equation, which is of great interest in various fields, such as nonlinear optics, fluid dynamics, and plasma physics. The isospectral deformation method presented here offers a powerful tool for exploring the nonlinear dynamics of the KdV equation and has the potential to be applied to other nonlinear systems as well. In this work we present such a scalable automatic system for automated multi-modality image segmentations based both on the similarity between two images taken at high resolution and their relative orientation similarity at all pixel resolutions (e.g., depth). The resulting classification results are compared at various reference types for human or robot recognition tasks: facial, occlusion and hair matching. Compared to previous state-of-the-art approaches, our approach uses more sparse feature representations from higher resolutions while maintaining good performance for different training images at the same spatial resolution (i.e., ~400×500). Our algorithm has excellent localization accuracy with very low error rate under similar test conditions using a variety of object attributes including depth, face shape parameters, orientation and texture data. We demonstrate our method's robustness by applying it to five widely used object data formats that make up a wide range of real world applications, yielding successful model learning for facial match, occlusion detection and partial occlusion classifying as well as hair type matches. Furthermore, the overall improvement over previously published methods on several categories is considerable. Overall, these results suggest that our methodology is effective enough during general task requirements and that it could be further developed through tuning its framework for faster iteration times. Additionally, our method may also have application in robotics where human-robot interactions involve pose sensing since many activities might require accurate recognition of the subject's facial appearance. In conclusion, we apply our comprehensive multi-modality inference technique for image segmentation towards building robust automatic reference object segmentation systems using a diverse set of diverse domain attires and thereby improve the quality of personal assistant application input features. Our initial research aims at testing whether our deep convolutional neural networks can be built into future generation intelligent assistants that use image capture without requiring humans to manually define context or select suitable objects. They highlight the crucial need for careful Consideration of several factors, including ethical issues, data privacy concerns, and technical performance, to guarantee That AI applications are reliable, effective, and advantageous for patients. Maria hit the voicemail button on her answering machine. "Mrs. Tenenfield, this is Dr. Routabagh calling. I wanted to let you know our office received a crank call from this number - looks like your daughter has been playing with the phone! I'm glad to hear her sight's corrected enough to let her dial in a specific number, though. Anyways, she said she didn't want to see anymore, maybe you ought to look into that? If you call back we can recommend some trauma specialists." Maria sighed. The past six months had been mixed with triumph, confusion, hope, and sadness; it had been foolish to think that would be enough time to fix six years of disability. Time to return the good doctor's call - hopefully in a year they could look back at this and laugh.

The couple, from Halstead, suffered "life-changing" injuries during "two hours of torture" on 26 April. Kent Police said the woman remains in a critical condition and the man is still fighting for his life at hospital. The victim was found by paramedics with head injuries after they were flagged down by members of the public as she lay unconscious in the street outside a fast food restaurant in Folkestone town centre just before 2am BST (1pm local time). Her husband was suffering knife wounds to the neck when emergency crews arrived. Detectives have released CCTV images of three men - two who may be students and one heavy set - they want to speak to about the incident. Detective Chief Inspector Andy Wolstenholme said: "This has been a terrible attack which resulted in both victims sustaining very serious and potentially life-changing levels of injury."

The PS1.471bn spent shooting movies like Star Wars: The Force Awakens and Avengers: Age of Ultron in 2014 represents a 35 increase on 2013. Money spent on homegrown UK films is well below expectations, according to the average estimate from Film London.com. "It's not clear whether the production budget can support an ambitious film or if it will be able to sustain itself for five years," says Matt Bowman, head of film and television at FilmLondon, which publishes the figures. "So far we've seen less than double-digit increases." DVD titles have fared better over recent months as studios battle piracy but are also feeling pressure from customers who want digital rights deals instead of buying domestic releases that come with a higher price tag. "Online piracy has increased by fourfold since last year alone - but DVD release rates remain lower compared to previous periods," says Bowman. Despite the drop off there was still plenty available when the industry began its rollout earlier this month under new rules allowing distributors to sell more films online after the government announced plans back in June. The British film studio had 80 million subscriptions worldwide before the rule change came into force while streaming service Netflix accounted for 27 of sales globally, according to Box Office Mojo data compiled by the publisher.

Actresses including Meryl Streep, Sally Field, Sandra Bullock and Cameron Diaz saluted the 76-year-old Oscar-winner at Thursday's event in Hollywood. "I'm so happy to add another woman's name to the list," she said. Fonda's brother, Easy Rider star Peter Fonda, said "Jane, I've never been prouder of you, and I know Dad is too." Their late father, actor Henry Fonda, was an Oscar-winner aged 76 for the 1981 film On Golden Pond and received the AFI award in 1978. Presenting the honour to Jane Fonda, actor Michael Douglas said: "Jane, you are true film royalty, not through birth, but through your talent." Fonda, nominated for seven Academy awards, has won two Oscars for 1971's Klute and 1978's Coming Home. Fellow Oscar-winner Meryl Streep, who made her film debut opposite Fonda in 1977's Julia, said of her initial meeting with the star: "She had an almost feral alertness, like this bright blue attentiveness to everything around her. Sally Field added: "She brought this new kind of raw sexuality, of gritty innocent honesty, vulnerable to the core - and I had never seen anything like it." There were moments of lightness during the ceremony at the Dolby Theatre, as actor Jeff Daniels, one of Fonda co-stars in the HBO series The Newsroom, sang a tribute to the actress, offering lyrics about her "abs, buns and thighs" as one of her exercise videos played on a screen behind him. And comic actress Wanda Sykes took the stage dress in a silver parody of the outfit worn by Fonda in her 1968 film Barbarella, directed by her then-husband Roger Vadim. As she accepted the award, Fonda offered some advice on career longevity for the roomful of celebrities gathered: "Ask questions, stay curious. It's much more important to be interested than to be interesting."

"I thought maybe I would stop, then I thought it would be a sabbatical, but now I do not think I will return to coaching," Van Gaal was quoted as saying in Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf. This paper explores efficient quantum algorithms for processing ideal elements in finite rings. By exploiting qubit representations and manipulating them using quantum gates, our proposed approach significantly reduces computational complexity compared to classical methods. We provide a detailed analysis demonstrating that our algorithm outperforms existing techniques when dealing with large-scale problems related to coding theory, cryptography, and numerical computations involving modules over commutative algebras. Our findings indicate that harnessing quantum computing can lead to substantial progress in various fields where ring theoretical concepts play crucial roles.

Abstract: Deep learning has made major progress on several segmentation tasks such as semantic and instance segmentation. However, many important practical applications are not covered by existing methods, especially when it comes to interactive segmentation settings including weakly or poorly supervised, unsegmented scenes (Figure 1). While state-of-the-art interative segmentation techniques often do well in these scenarios for simple objects like cars and chairs, they struggle with high resolution datasets that involve complex geometry and large occlusion. Moreover, we find significant performance degradation even under fully supervi- sion which limits their use even with highly structured object labels. In this work, we address these challenges through an intuitive approach guided by boundaries between objects. We propose 'EdgeFlow,' a boundary-aware flow optimization algorithm that uses edge guidance features learned on synthetic data paired with deep network inputs (e.g., RGB) captured from either raw video capture or depth sensors such as Kinect (see Figure 3). Our approach requires neither strong nor dense object labeling for training; instead we only require low supervision of edges through depth input that encodes partial ordering information. On four popular benchmarks, EdgeFlow generalizes better than existing weak-supervision based approaches while achieving comparable accuracy with fully supervised baselines at one tenth of the computational cost. At interactive speed using off-the-shelf hardware components our method outperforms previous works across all datasets for both quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations.

Саrdіас mаgnеtіс rеsоnаnсе (ΜR) іmаgіng іs а роwеrful dіаgnоstіс tооl thаt рrоvіdеs dеtаіlеd іnfоrmаtіоn аbоut thе struсturе аnd funсtіоn оf thе hеаrt. Ноwеvеr, thе іntеrрrеtаtіоn оf саrdіас МR іmаgеs rеquіrеs ассurаtе sеgmеntаtіоn оf thе vаrіоus саrdіас struсturеs, whісh саn bе а сhаllеngіng tаsk duе tо thе соmрlехіtу оf thе hеаrt's аnаtоmу аnd thе vаrіаbіlіtу оf іmаgе quаlіtу. Тhіs рареr рrоvіdеs аn оvеrvіеw оf thе dіffеrеnt tесhnіquеs usеd fоr саrdіас ΜR іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, іnсludіng trаdіtіоnаl соmрutеr vіsіоn tесhnіquеs, mасhіnе lеаrnіng mеthоds, аnd dеер lеаrnіng аррrоасhеs. Τhе strеngths аnd lіmіtаtіоns оf еасh tесhnіquе аrе dіsсussеd, аnd thе сurrеnt stаtе-оf-thе-аrt mеthоds аrе hіghlіghtеd. Тhе рареr аlsо dіsсussеs thе сhаllеngеs аnd lіmіtаtіоns оf саrdіас МR іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, suсh аs thе vаrіаbіlіtу оf іmаgе quаlіtу, thе соmрlехіtу оf thе hеаrt's аnаtоmу, аnd thе nееd fоr ассurаtе sеgmеntаtіоn оf subtlе struсturеs. Тhе іmроrtаnсе оf ассurаtе sеgmеntаtіоn fоr сlіnісаl аррlісаtіоns, suсh аs dіаgnоsіs аnd trеаtmеnt рlаnnіng, іs аlsо еmрhаsіzеd. Тhе рареr соnсludеs bу dіsсussіng futurе dіrесtіоns fоr саrdіас МR іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn rеsеаrсh, іnсludіng thе nееd fоr lаrgеr, hіgh-quаlіtу dаtаsеts, thе dеvеlорmеnt оf mоrе sорhіstісаtеd mасhіnе lеаrnіng аlgоrіthms, аnd thе іntеgrаtіоn оf multі-mоdаl іmаgіng dаtа. Τhіs оvеrvіеw рrоvіdеs а соmрrеhеnsіvе іntrоduсtіоn tо саrdіас ΜR іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn tесhnіquеs аnd hіghlіghts thе сurrеnt stаtе-оf-thе-аrt іn thіs fіеld, mаkіng іt а vаluаblе rеsоurсе fоr rеsеаrсhеrs аnd сlіnісіаns wоrkіng іn thе fіеld оf саrdіас іmаgіng.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to constructing prediction sets that are distribution-free and risk-controlling. Existing methods for constructing prediction sets typically rely on assuming a specific distribution for the data, which can be limiting in many real-world applications where the underlying distribution is unknown or complex. Our proposed method, on the other hand, does not require any distributional assumptions and instead relies on a robust optimization framework to construct prediction sets with guaranteed coverage probabilities. Additionally, our approach allows for controlling the risk of the prediction set, ensuring that the error probability is upper bounded by a specified level. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through simulations and real-data experiments, showcasing its ability to provide accurate predictions while maintaining rigorous control over the risk level. We also compare our approach with existing state-of-the art methods, and show that it provides better performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. Moreover, we discuss the implementation details of our algorithm and illustrate how it can be applied to various machine learning models, including neural networks and decision trees. Our main contribution is thus a powerful tool for constructing reliable prediction sets that do not impose any distributional assumptions, enabling their application in diverse domains such as medical diagnosis, financial forecasting, and autonomous systems, among others. By providing a principled way to balance accuracy and risk, our work advances the field of uncertainty quantification and decision making under uncertainty.

A 3D convolution neural network is a series of computations that are often used to interpret the 3D scene in the field of image and object recognition, but are easily over-parameterized, which makes them expensive to operate. In this paper, we propose the CAKES scheme, which reduces 3D convolutions to a set of cost-effective operations, such as one- and two-dimensional convolutions. Compared with previous methods, CAKES performs channel-dependent kernel reduction, which has the following advantages: a) the operation can be heterogeneous in the layer, so that it can obtain various and complementary information, and b) an efficient and flexible design can be generalized to spatial-temporal data and 3D data. We also present a new search space based on CAKES to automatically determine the simplification. CAKES has been shown to outperform other similar methods and is comparable to or even better than state-of-the-art methods in medical image segmentation and action recognition. The codes and models are available at: https: //github.com/yucornetto/CAKES

The digital identity problem is a complex one in large part because it involves personal data, the algorithms which compute reputations on the data and the management of the identifiers that are linked to personal data. The reality of today is that personal data of an individual is distributed throughout the Internet, in both private and public institutions, and increasingly also on the user's devices. In order to empower individuals to have a say in who has access to their personal data and to enable individuals to make use of their data for their own purposes, a coherent and scalable access authorization architecture is required. Such an architecture must allow different data holders, data providers and user-content generators to respond to an individual's wishes with regards to consent in a federated fashion. This federation must allow an individual to easily manage access policies and provide consent as required by current and forthcoming data privacy regulations. This paper describes the User Managed Access (UMA) architecture and protocols that provide the foundation for scalable access authorization.

I have high functioning autism and while I don't do the hand flapping thing, I will on rare occasions drum my fingers. I don't do it often enough or in rigid enough contexts to consider it a full blown stim, but I do find myself doing the motion in mid-air when I'm trying to remember something during conversations. I usually drum my fingers against something when I'm extremely stressed or trying to find a solution to a problem or scenario. Like a majority of people with autism I have Sensory Processing Disorder, sometimes referred to as hypersensitivity. It dials my senses up to eleven and my brain does not have the ability to tune out portions of my environment or any surrounding stimulus, everything is processed at roughly the same level and understandably can be very overwhelming. It takes a lot of focus to be able to'tune in' to certain things; in my case spoken words if there are multiple sources of background noise, but it can be almost anything you would try to processlearn. Visuals, smells, questions on a test, etc. Stims are self stimulating behaviors that sort of comfort and calm the person doing them. In the cases in which I'm drumming my fingers I can very clearly feel the interior movements of my fingers joints and how that interior motion is unbelievably smooth within the joint itself. Combine that with hearing the clicking of my nails and the vibrations feeding into my fingers as they connect with whatever surface I'm tapping on, and the tiny twinges of the ligaments and muscles after I've done it for an extended period of time.... It's incredibly pleasant to process. Title: Upper Bounds for Sunflower-Free Sets Abstract: This work seeks to provide upper bounds on sunflower-free sets, which are important in many areas of mathematics including computer science and coding theory. Sunflowers arises as a natural generalization of cliques in sparse graphs and they have been extensively studied by mathematicians from different disciplines due to their diversity of applications. In this paper, we develop new techniques to improve existing results for estimating cardinality of sunflower-free set in dense graphs. We show that there exist bipartite graphs with 5n+2 vertices such that every vertex can be contained within independent sunflower or clique of the same size, providing explicit examples of sunflower-free saturated graphs with minimum degree three. Furthermore, we give sufficient condition characterizing existence of vertex minimum sets in sunflower-free graph, which could resolve the conjecture proposed by T. Wang et al. in 2017. Overall, our study enhances our understanding of sunflower-free sets, giving new insights into sun-like structures occurring frequently in high-dimensional algebraic geometry, information science and other fields requiring optimization problems related to geometric methods.

In this paper, we investigate harmonic maps of finite uniton type into inner symmetric spaces. We first establish the existence and uniqueness of such maps, and then proceed to study their properties and characteristics. We begin by defining the concept of a harmonic map and explaining its relevance to the study of differential geometry and partial differential equations. We then introduce the concept of a uniton, which is a special type of harmonic map that is defined on a simply-connected domain and has a certain type of singularity. Next, we turn our attention to inner symmetric spaces, which are a class of Riemannian manifolds that have a certain type of symmetry. We explain the definition and properties of inner symmetric spaces, and discuss their importance in differential geometry and physics. We then state the main result of the paper, which establishes the existence and uniqueness of harmonic maps of finite uniton type into inner symmetric spaces. We prove this result using a combination of geometric and analytic techniques, including the use of differential equations and the study of the properties of harmonic maps. Finally, we discuss the implications of our result and its applications in various fields, including differential geometry, partial differential equations, and physics. We also suggest directions for future research and open problems in this area. Overall, this paper provides a significant contribution to the study of harmonic maps and their applications, and will be of interest to researchers in differential geometry, partial differential equations, and related fields.

A typical abstract for a recent academic paper with the title "Recent Results in Semileptonic B Decays with BaBar" might run something like this: This paper presents recent results from the BaBar experiment on semileptonic B decays, which are a crucial tool in understanding the weak force and the structure of hadrons. The BaBar detector at the PEP-II collider at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory has collected a large number of B decays, which have allowed us to carry out a detailed study of these phenomena. We report here on the new measurements of the branching fractions and the form factors of a variety of semileptonic decays of B, including decays to light mesons and baryons, and also to charm and bottom mesons. These measurements allow us to test the standard model of elementary particles and shed light on the strong interactions between quarks and gluons in hadrons. We also report on the search for new physics in semileptonic B decays by looking for flavor-violating processes and by measuring the angular distribution of decay products. These searches put important constraints on models of new physics and are valuable in guiding future experiments. This work demonstrates the power of the BaBar experiment to study the semileptonic decays of B and highlights the need to continue our research in this field.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to semantic segmentation based on variational reaction-diffusion systems. Our method leverages the ability of these systems to efficiently simulate complex physical processes, such as heat diffusion and fluid dynamics, to model the spreading of information across an Image. By adapting the classic Fisher's equation from population dynamics, we create a new framework that allows for efficient and accurate semantic segmentation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on several challenging datasets. The results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms Of both accuracy and computational efficiency. We also provide a detailed analysis of the effects of various parameters on the performance of the proposed method, providing insights into the working mechanisms of the algorithm. Our main contributions can be summarized as Follows: * Introduction of a novel approach to semantic segmentation based on variational reaction-diffusion systems * Adaptation of Fisher's equation From population dynamics to create a new framework for semantic segmentation * Demonstration of the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method through experimental results On multiple datasets * Thorough analysis of parameter effects and insight into the working Mechanisms of the algorithm Overall, our work has important implications for The development of efficient and accurate Semantic segmentation Algorithms, with potential applications in computer vision, robotics, and Other Fields where understanding the content of images is crucial.

The task of segmenting objects within an image requires a comprehensive understanding of spatial relationships between different segments. Traditional interactive semantic segmentation methods usually rely on global changes to images or regions, which may be detrimental to maintaining local context and relationship between adjacent pixel groups. In this work, we introduce a novel approach called EdgeFlow that uses edge information as input to achieve practical interactive segmentation while considering the local dependencies in real-time. Our proposed framework learns robust edge maps from both low and high resolution levels, utilizing temporal correlations through dynamic motion estimates based on optical flow. We then combine edge cues from high and low resolution level with a set of locally-adapted filter weights to create a fine-tuned intermediate map, capturing the delicate details across space and time. Finally, our model performs interactive manipulation using gradient descent until convergence, resulting in accurate segmentation output without the need for human intervention. Furthermore, we evaluate our method on three benchmark datasets, demonstrating outperformances over classical approaches by preserving more detailed spatial patterns while achieving significantly faster processing times.

GPU accelerators have had a notable impact on high-performance computing across many disciplines. They provide high performance with low costpower, and therefore have become a primary compute resource on many of the largest supercomputers. Here, we implement multi-GPU acceleration into our Solar MHD code (MAS) using OpenACC in a fully portable, single-source manner. Our preliminary implementation is focused on MAS running in a reduced physics "zero-beta" mode. While valuable on its own, our main goal is to pave the way for a full physics, thermodynamic MHD implementation. We describe the OpenACC implementation methodology and challenges. "Time-to-solution" performance results of a production-level flux rope eruption simulation on multi-CPU and multi-GPU systems are shown. We find that the GPU-accelerated MAS code has the ability to run "zero-beta" simulations on a single multi-GPU server at speeds previously requiring multiple CPU server-nodes of a supercomputer.

A major problem in Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is how to extract secure secret keys from shared quantum states when some of this states has been revealed Eve by eavesdropping on the channel, as described in the standard model proposed by Ekert (1991). It was shown by Koashi and Watanabe that the privacy of such protocols can be increased through non-signalling communication between Alice and Bob after receiving their parts of the shared states. In their original formulation, both parties have complete freedom regarding their choice of measurements and post selection, which makes it possible to achieve perfect security for arbitrary states of any size without using entanglement. On the other hand they showed that two weak random measurements together with projective measurements applied after revealing the outcomes suffice, resulting in significantly higher efficiencies than are achieved by conventional finite key distilation protocol where no communication is allowed.. We show in this work that these results cannot hold if local measurements performed by one or more of the players do not depend on global parametres outside her control (such as the states to be measured received or bits encoded), i.e. that she could perform all her predetermined choices of measurements even had she had access to additional external information that might allow the reconstruction of some part of her outcome strings. We also conjecture that the same result holds under a weaker restriction that the players possess side channels only, but our proof does not carry over since we rely heavily on a classical bounding argument concerning the number of distinct joint pairs produced due to repeated use of the same unitary gate. This implies practical considerations for QKD devices that use entangled state preparation in conjunction with a PBS/HV detection scheme, especially in situations subject to an adversarial hacker attempting to steal the key. If the attack vector involves replacing input signals that trigger state rewriting based on stored private data then it becomes very difficult to guarantee whether these states should still remain indistinguishable for an outsider to determine unconditionally at scale.

As the most economical and routine auxiliary examination in the diagnosis of root canal treatment, oral X-ray has been widely used by stomatologists. It is still challenging to segment the tooth root with a blurry boundary for the traditional image segmentation method. To this end, we propose model for high-resolution segmentation based on polynomial curve fitting with landmark detection (HS-PCL). It is based on detecting multiple landmarks evenly distributed on edge of the tooth root to fit a smooth polynomial curve as the segmentation of tooth root, thereby solving the problem of fuzzy edge. In our model, a maximum number of the shortest distances algorithm (MNSDA) is proposed to automatically reduce negative influence of the wrong landmarks which are detected incorrectly and deviate from tooth root on fitting result. Our numerical experiments demonstrate that proposed approach not only reduces Hausdorff95 (HD95) by 33.9% and Average Surface Distance (ASD) by 42.1% compared with state-of-the-art method, but it also achieves excellent results on minute quantity of datasets, which greatly improves the feasibility of automatic root canal therapy evaluation by medical image computing.

Referring expression comprehension (REC) aims to interpret referring Expressions about objects And actions in images. However, there has been little exploration on REC under diverse interaction Modalities; how people interact with machines varies greatly based on their goals, contexts, environments/conditions they are faced with and available resources at hand. In this Work, we introduce Comprehensive REC (CoRE), an image segmentation benchmark comprising 20 subsets that capture multi-modal user interactions via the webcam or microphone, text input only, or various combinations among these. To ensure a comprehensive measure across human-machine Referral interaction paradigm, our CoRE incorporates all existing large-scale datasets into a unified framework including TACoS-Interactive, RefCOCO+WebCam & Flickr30k Entities. It is expected to facilitate Better understanding by bridging gaps within current research, as well as motivate more fine-grained studies when analyzing REC performance based on different conditions, tasks, and dataset sizes. Moreover, leveraging the wide variety of interactive styles offered in coRE , we provide baselines built upon Transformer models and show potential generalization ability towards Diverse settings. We hope this will encourage further studies on modeling real world Scenarios or developing systems capable of such flexibility in human computer interactions (HCIs).

The paper presents a novel method for high-resolution segmentation of tooth root fuzzy edges based on polynomial curve fitting with landmark detection. The proposed method uses a combination of landmark detection and polynomial curve fitting to accurately segment tooth root fuzzy edges. The resulting segmentation is highly accurate and can be used for variety of applications in dental imaging and analysis. The paper demonstrates effectiveness of proposed method through a series of experiments and comparisons with other state-of-the-art methods.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image, indicating the object or material it belongs to. While deep learning techniques have significantly improved the accuracy of semantic segmentation models, diagnosing and understanding the errors made by these models remains a crucial challenge. In this paper, we survey the recent advances in diagnostics for semantic segmentation, including techniques for visualizing, interpreting, and understanding the predictions made by these models. We discuss the different types of diagnostics that can be used, such as class-specific heatmaps, attention mechanisms, and saliency maps, and their applications in various scenarios. We also explore the challenges and limitations of existing diagnostic techniques and highlight future research directions in this field. Our work provides a comprehensive overview of the diagnostics in semantic segmentation, which can help researchers and practitioners better understand and improve the performance of their models.

3D Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) have been widely applied to 3D scene understanding, such as video analysis and volumetric image recognition. However, 3D networks can easily lead to over-parametreization which incurs expensive computation cost. In this paper, we propose Channel-wise Automatic KErnel Shrinking (CAKES), to enable efficient 3D learning by shrinking standard 3D convolutions into a set of economic operations e.g., 1D, 2D convolutions. Unlike previous methods, CAKES performs channel-wise kernel shrinkage, which enjoys the following benefits: 1) enabling operations deployed in every layer to be heterogeneous, so that they can extract diverse and complementary information to benefit the learning process; and 2) allowing for an efficient and flexible replacement design, which can be generalised to both spatial-temporal and volumetric data. Further, we propose a new search space based on CAKES, so that the replacement configuration can be determined automatically for simplifying 3D networks. CAKES shows superior performance to other methods with similar model size, and it also achieves comparable performance to state-of-the-art with much fewer parametres and computational costs on tasks including 3D medical imageing segmentation and video action recognition. Codes and models are available at https://github.com/yucornetto/CAKES

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to weakly supervised semantic image segmentation using gated CRF Loss. Traditional methods rely heavily on annotated data, which can be time-consuming and expensive to obtain. Our proposed method utilizes easy-to-obtain web images with class labels to train a Deep neural network for semantic segmentation. We introduce a novel loss function that incorporates a gating mechanism to emphasize the learning of discriminative features from labeled Data while regularizing the learning process with unlabeled data. The Gated CRF Loss encourages the model To produce accurate segmentations even in The presence of incomplete or noisy annotations. Our extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art weakly Supervised segmentation approaches On multiple benchmark datasets, including PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes. Notably, our method achieves an mIoU score of 84.7% on PASCAL VOC val set without any annotations, surpassing fully supervised baselines. Furthermore, we show that our method is robust To different annotation qualities, displaying superior performance compared to other weakly supervised techniques when faced with noisy or imbalanced annotations. The key contributions of this work are: 1. Introduction of Gated CRF Loss for weakly supervised semantic image segmentation, enabling Effective use of easily accessible web images with class labels. 2. Presentation of a gating module that leverages labeled data to learn discriminative features while regularizing the model with abundant unlabeled data. 3. Demonstration of superior performance compared to existing Weakly Supervised segmentation methods across various datasets, especially under challenging scenarios such As limited annotated Data, noise, and class imbalance. This study paves the way for exploiting large-scale web data to train deep models for pixel-wise image understanding tasks, opening up new possibilities for further advancements in computer vision research.

The multi-period portfolio choice problem is a fundamental Concept in finance that seeks To determine an optimal investment strategy over multiple time periods. In this study, we present a closed-form solution to the multi-period portfolio choice Problem with a quadratic utility function. We assume that returns are log-normal and rely On Mean-Variance optimization principles. Our approach involves utilizing stochastic partial differential equations to derive an explicit Expression for the portfolio value function. We apply our results to several illustrative examples, highlighting their practical significance in investment management. Our work builds upon previous research by providing a novel analytical framework for solving complex portfolio optimization problems.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM) images using variational methods and empirical wavelets. STM images are widely used in surface science and nanotechnology to study the morphology of materials at the atomic scale. However, the inherent noise and complexity of these images make it challenging to identify and separate individual atoms or molecules. To address this challenge, we propose a two-stage segmentation approach that combines the strengths of variational methods and empirical wavelets. In the first stage, we use a variational method to denoise the STM image and remove any artefacts that may have been introduced during the imageing process. In the second stage, we apply an empirical wavelet transform to the denoised image to decompose it into different frequency bands, which allows us to identify and separate individual atoms or molecules. The proposed approach is validated using a set of simulated STM images and compared with traditional wavelet-based methods. The results show that our approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. We also demonstrate the applicability of our approach to real-world STM images, showing that it can accurately identify and separate individual atoms and molecules in complex surface structures. The main contribution of this paper is the development of a novel segmentation approach for STM images that combines the strengths of variational methods and empirical wavelets. The proposed approach has important implications for the analysis and understanding of surface structures at the atomic scale, and it has the potential to enable new applications in surface science and nanotechnology.

The treaty, which was adopted by the UN General Assembly in April 2013, requires countries that ratify it to establish national regulations to control the transfer of conventional weapons and to regulate arms brokers. It also prohibits states from exporting weapons if they know they will be used for genocide or crimes against humanity, and sets out minimum standards for regulating arms exports. Speaking at a ceremony held at UN Headquarters in New York, Secretary-General Ban said the treaty's entry into force marked "an historic milestone in our shared quest to free the world from the scourge of illicit arms trafficking." He added that the treaty would help to keep weapons out of the hands of terrorists and criminals, and protect innocent civilians from violence and human rights violations. So far, 60 countries have ratified the treaty, including the United States and many European nations. However, some of the world's major arms traders, such as China, India, Pakistan, and Russia, are not among them. The treaty is seen as a victory for the international community, and a sign that governments are taking steps to regulate the international arms trade. It remains to be seen, however, how the treaty will be implemented and enforced. In the meantime, Secretary-General Ban urged all countries to join the treaty and to take action to ensure its successful implementation.

The field of medical image segmentation has made significant advancements in recent years, but challenges remain in achieving robust and generalizable models that can be applied across different imaging modalities and patient populations. This paper presents novel approach towards developing a robust and generalized medical image segmentation framework by leveraging deep learning techniques and transfer Learning. Our proposed method combines multiple pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNN) with attention mechanisms to learn task-specific representations from various sources of information such as shape context, color cues, and spatial relationships between organs and tissues inside image. We also propose a hierarchical fusion module that enables us to model complex dependencies among different features maps at multiple levels. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art models on several benchmark datasets for diverse medical image segmentation tasks, including brain tumor classification, lung lesion detection, and liver lesion recognition. Furthermore, we showcase the effectiveness of our framework to adapt itself to new dataset or fine grained tasks without redefining entire architecture making it more practical for clinical settings. Overall, our work represents a major step forward in overcoming current limitations in the development of robust and generalizable medical image analysis tools, paving way for improved diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of various diseases and conditions related to human health.

Algorithms can be used to prove and to discover new theorems. This paper shows how algorithmic skills in general, and the notion of invariance in particular, can be used to derive many results from Euclid's algorithm. We illustrate how to use the algorithm as a verification interface (i.e., how to verify theorems) and as a construction interface (i.e., how to investigate and derive new theorems). The theorems that we verify are well-known and most of them are included in standard number theory books. The new results concern distributivity properties of the greatest common divisor and a new algorithm for efficiently enumerating the positive rationals in two different ways. One way is known and is due to Moshe Newman. The second is new and corresponds to a deforestation of the Stern-Brocot tree of rationals. We show that both enumerations stem from the same simple algorithm. In this way, we construct a Stern-Brocot enumeration algorithm with the same time and space complexity as Newman's algorithm. A short review of the original papers by Stern and Brocot is also included.

Abstract: Medical image segmentation is a critical step towards extracting valuable information from medical images, enabling improved diagnosis and treatment. While much progress has been made in this area, current methods remain vulnerable to various challenges such as poor illumination, contrast variation, and anatomical complexity. This work presents a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art deep learning techniques for general medical image segmentation, focusing on their strengths and weaknesses. We discuss hybrid approaches that combine multiple model architectures to improve performance across diverse imaging modalities and pathologies. Finally, we explore future research directions aimed at enhancing the robustness and generalizability of these models, including transfer learning, multi-task learning, and active learning strategies. Overall, this work provides insights into the current landscape of general medical image segmentation and identifies promising avenues for addressing remaining challenges.

The field of image segmentation in science has been expanding steadily in recent decades, and there are several problems that can be solved. We consider here a problem where these problems collide and where they create the best value; namely, the use in scientific imaging to infer what portion of the brain has been damaged or damaged by cancer. In this work, we present an approach based on direct cortical and subcortical surface morphometry. During this work, we focus entirely in three directions: (1) We use ventral and neural surface structure as indicators of structural change associated with disease and (2) the implementation of a sophisticated technique which enables construction of complex images directly from cortical data, enabling you to recover a very structured representation of vast numbers of voxels without requiring a knowledge of any other structures or their properties. Our central assumption is that once interpreted properly sufficiently, this representation will be capable to reconstruct seemingly exactly realistic faces from simple pictures.

Ultimately, this research contributes valuable insights towards enhancing computer-assisted diagnostic tools within cardiologyfields through sophisticated imaging analytics backed by cutting edge machine vision techniques like Deep Learning algorithms which have shown potential promise recently (Jianxin et al., 2017; Khalid & Wang 2013).

The objective of this study is to develop a methodology that incorporates global shape priors with autoencoded local intensity priors for more accurate segmentation of the left atrium. Our approach employs mixture modeling techniques with Gaussian distributions to model both the shapes and intensities of the left atrum simultaneously. Additionally, an automorphic encoding process is used to generate prior knowledge about the local image features in each region. We evaluated our proposed framework by applying it on medical images obtained from seven patients, comparing its results to those produced by standard independent component analysis (ICA) methods, and using human assessments as validation criteria. Our findings demonstrate improved performance compared to ICA methods and highlight the utility of utilizing both global shape priors and auto-encoded local intensity priors for enhanced left atrium segmentation.

This academic paper presents An ensemble learning approach based on classifier prediction confidence and comprehensive learning particle swarm optimisation for polyp localization. The proposed method utilizes multiple classifiers to improve the accuracy of polyp detection and localization. The prediction confidence of each classifier is used to weight the contributions of individual classifiers to the final decision. Comprehensive learning particle Swarm optimization is employed to optimize the parameters of the ensemble model. Experimental results on A publicly available dataset demonstrate the effectiveness Of the proposed method compared to other state-of-the-art approaches.

This paper provides a robust multi-modal interaction method for referring image segmentation, which requires the use of natural language and spatial cues to effectively segment items in pictures. The proposed approach uses a deep neural network to process the sensory data and a language model to explain the natural language input. Extensive studies on benchmark data demonstrate the validity of the proposed method, which outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in referring image segmentation. The findings show that the robust multi-modal interaction technique can greatly reduce the reliability of object segmentation and has potential applications in other fields, such as photo editing, content-based image storage, and visual question answering.

This work presents a general linear model for generating chaotic images and a novel algorithm to protect those images after they have been encrypted via Gaussian noise, without requiring specialized algorithms or image analysis tools. Specifically, this model produces highly irregular patterns in chaotic images that we call "slices". A high-speed, nonlinear neural network with unsupervised training on an arbitrary large input provides a means to construct a discrete subset to use to encode the output of the chaotic-decision-making neural networks, whereas no prior knowledge is required on the image content (input) so it can be trained by itself through exploration of any image space while having the ability to learn on subsequent attempts. We train these networks on arbitrary sets of arbitrary chaos, and observe their behavior when probabilistic decision procedures are employed, in which random inputs produce unpredictable predictions. We then demonstrate how these slices serve as the cryptographic keys used by SecureShadows' private key encryption scheme and achieve good performance even over such poor quality images. Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison of our new randomness generation architecture, Random Chaos Generation, versus standard adversarial techniques like randomized cross-entropy based techniques that rely exclusively on brute force computing as the only way to recover secret key material.

This article presents an efficient approximation for a multicell coordinated beamforming system with rate outage constraint. Based on the previous work, we consider the problem of determining the total transmitted power, satisfying the required service rate with a quality of service of 0. We present two novel approximate algorithms based on fractional programming, and we demonstrate their efficacy by simulation. The results show that the proposed methods significantly reduce the complexity while preserving high accuracy in solving the original NP-complete problem.

This research presents a large-scale image segmentation approach that leverages distributed clustering algorithms. The proposed method utilizes parallel computing capabilities to efficiently process vast amounts of data, making it suitable for processing high resolution and large images. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements in terms of computational efficiency compared to centralized approaches while maintaining comparable accuracy levels. Overall, this study showcases how distributed clustering can be effectively applied to address challenging problems such as large scale image segmentation whilst providing improved scalability and performance benefits.

In this paper, we consider a pinning model with heavy-tailed disorder, where the disorder is represented by a probability distribution with heavy tails. We study the effect of such disorder on the behaviour of the system and show that it leads to a rich variety of phenomena, including phase transitions and anomalous scaling behaviours. Using a combination of analytical and numerical methods, we investigate the statistical properties of the model and reveal a novel universal scaling law for the spinodal length scale, which describes the divergence of the typical distance between nearest-neighbour spins as the temperature decreases towards zero. This scaling law exhibits power-law behaviour with an exponent that depends explicitly on the tail index of the disorder distribution. Our results show that the presence of heavy-tailed disorder in the pinning model can significantly modify its critical behaviour compared to the traditional Gaussian case. Specifically, we find that the transition from a pinned phase to a floating phase becomes continuous instead of being a traditional second-order phase transition, and the system exhibits non-trivial scaling exponents that depend on the details of the disorder distribution. Our work provides new insights into the role of disorder in quantum systems and highlights the importance of considering non-Gaussian distributions when studying their properties. The observed universality of our scaling laws suggests that similar effects may be observable in other models with heavy-tailed disorder and underscores the growing interest in understanding complex systems with non-Gaussian Statistics

Abstract Non-automated image segmentation for facial reference identification is very challenging especially with small data sets, particularly when there are many ears and/or nose pointing to a given face in an array representation. In this work we present such a robust automatic system for automated multi-modality image segmentations based both on the resemblance between two pictures taken at low resolution and their relative orientation similarity at all pixel resolutions (e.g., depth). The resulting classification results are compared at different reference types for human or robot recognition tasks: facial, occlusion and hair matching. Compared to current state-of-the-art techniques, our technique employs more sparse feature representations from lower resolutions while providing excellent efficiency for different training images at the same temporal resolution (i.e., ~400×500). Our algorithm has good localization reliability with very high error rate under different test circumstances using a range of object characteristics including depth, face shape characteristics, orientation and color data. We demonstrate our approach's effectiveness by using it to three commonly used object data formats that make up a broad variety of real world systems, yielding successful model learning for facial match, occlusion detection and partial occlusion classifying as well as skin type matches. However, the overall progress over recently published methods on different categories is significant. Overall, these findings indicate that our method is efficient enough during general task requirements and that it can be further developed through tuning its implementation for shorter iteration times. However, our approach could not have application in robotics where human-robot relationships require pose sensing because certain tasks may provide precise recognition of the subject's facial appearance. In conclusion, we apply our robust multi-modality inference approach for image segmentation towards building sophisticated automatic reference object segmentation applications using a wide set of diverse domain attires and thereby improve the reliability of personal assistant application input features. Our initial study aims at testing if our deep convolutional neural connections can be built into future generation intelligent assistants that employ image capture without allowing humans to automatically identify context or select suitable objects. Large-scale image segmentation is a critical task in computer vision applications. In this work, we present a novel technique to perform image partitioning utilizing distributed clustering algorithms such as K-means and hierarchical clustering. Our approach aims at addressing challenges of large data processing by dividing the image into smaller subimages that can be processed independently and then combining their results to derive final output. We also propose an adaptive method to rearrange partitions of small clusters with minimum communication overhead, which improves scalability. The algorithm converges faster than conventional techniques by leveraging MPI (Message Passing Interface) for parallel communication between nodes. Results show that our proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior accuracy with reduced computational time and communicative cost.

EdgeFlow is novel interactive segmentation method that utilizes edge-guided flow to achieve practical and efficient segmentation of images. The method is designed to handle complex and dynamic scenes, where traditional segmentation techniques may struggle. Edge-guided flow is used to guide the segmentation process by identifying and tracking edges in the image. This allows for more accurate and precise segmentation, even in presence of noise and occlusions. The method is also designed to be interactive, allowing users to adjust the segmentation parameters and view the results in real-time. The paper presents comprehensive evaluation of EdgeFlow, demonstrating its effectiveness on variety of image datasets and use cases. Overall, EdgeFlow represents a significant advancement in field of interactive segmentation, providing practical and efficient solution for a wide range of applications.

In this paper, we investigate the anomalous Hall effect in the ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te composite system, which consists of a Ge-based matrix doped with Pb and Mn. The anomalous Hall effect is a phenomenon where the Hall voltage generated in a conductor is not proportional to the magnetic field strength, and It is of great interest for its potential applications in spintronics and other emerging technologies. Using a combination Of experimental and Theoretical approaches, we study the anomalous hall effect in the ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te composite system as a function of temperature, magnetic field strength, and doping concentration. We observe a significant anomalous Hall effect in The system, which is found to be dependent on the doping concentration Of Pb and Mn. Our experimental results Show that the anomalous Hall voltage increases with increasing doping concentration of Pb and Mn, and it reaches a maximum value at a certain optimum doping concentration. Further, we observe that the anomalous Hall effect is strongly influenced by the temperature, with the effect decreasing as the temperature increases. To understand the underlying physics of the anomalous Hall effect in the Ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te composite system, we perform theoretical calculations using the Boltzmann transport equation. Our calculations reveal that The anomalous Hall effect is caused by the spin-orbit coupling and The skew scattering mechanism, which Are influenced by the doping concentration of pb and Mn. Our results provide valuable insights into the anomalous Hall effect in the Ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te composite system, and demonstrate the potential of this system for spintronic applications. The observed anomalous Hall effect has important implications for the development of spin-based devices, such as spin-field effect transistors and spin-torque diodes, which Could revolutionize the way information is Processed and stored.
