In a major development, the massive antitrust investigation against Google by various US states is expanding to include the search giant's business practices related to its search and Android businesses. According to sources, the investigation, which began in 2019, has intensified in recent months as more states have joined in. Currently, 39 states are part of the probe, which is looking into whether Google's dominance in the digital advertising market has led to anticompetitive behavior that harms consumers and stifles innovation. The expanded probe will focus on two key areas: Google's search algorithms and its Android operating system. The investigation will examine whether the company is using its market position to unfairly promote its own apps and services over those of its competitors. In particular, the probes will look at Google's agreements with smartphone manufacturers that require them to pre-install Google services on their devices, such as Google Search and Chrome. The investigators will also examine whether Google uses its control over the Android platform to disadvantage rival search engines and other competing apps. Experts suggest that these investigations could result in major legal action against Google, and could potentially lead to the breakup of the company or significant changes to how it operates. "This is a critical moment for our economy and for consumers," said Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who is leading the investigation. "There is nothing wrong with a business becoming the biggest game in town if it does so through free-market competition, but we have seen evidence that Google's business practices may have undermined competition and stifled innovation." Google has denied any wrongdoing and maintains that it operates in an open and competitive market. However, the company has already faced substantial fines from the European Union over antitrust violations related to its search and Android businesses. The investigation is still ongoing, and it remains to be seen how it will ultimately impact Google and the broader tech industry. However, it is clear that the stakes are high, and the outcome could have far-reaching implications for the future of online search and digital advertising.

We present an approach to training deep generative models that learns large sparse non-stationary distributions for the input features in image processing problems. To solve these problem we employ coarse-and-fine convolutional neural network. The model consists of two layers with separate hidden states; one layer generates the high-dimensional features while the other provides the low-dimensional perceptrons on top of which the high-resolution feature is computed. This allows us to train a large network whose structure consists of two recurrent connections to each hidden node through an arbitrary multilayer feedforward process (such as forward pass followed by back propagation). Our main inspiration was inspired by the famous Krizhevsky–Lehoux architecture of VGG. We show how our algorithm can be used to learn efficient and scalable multi-scale filters at scales greater than even the computational power available today. (Image courtesy of Wikipedia Commons)

The academic paper titled "FUTURE-AI: Guiding principles and Consensus recommendations for Trustworthy artificial Intelligence in Future Medical Imaging" presents a set of guiding principles and consensus recommendations for the development and implementation of trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) in medical Imaging. The paper emphasizes the importance of AI in improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical diagnosis and treatment, while also acknowledging The potential risks and challenges associated with the use of AI in healthcare. The paper proposes a set of guiding principles and recommendations that aim to ensure the responsible and ethical development and use of AI in medical imaging, including transparency, accountability, And patient-centeredness. Overall, the paper provides valuable insights and guidance for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers involved in the development and implementation of AI in medical imaging.

The asymptotic properties of functions have been studied by many mathematicians and physicists, in order to analyse the generating series of combinatorial objects whose enumeration can be related to physical models by partition formulas. In the present paper we investigate the case where the coefficients of the sum converge to those of the general term, for an infinite family of combinatorial systems defined by several parameters (which corresponds to considering smoothing at every variable). Our previous work on this subject gives us sufficient conditions to obtain results which are nearly sharp, under certain sufficiently general assumptions. We now develop a programme which is intended to provide as rapid an improvement as possible, in reachable cases, when the system is near the boundaries or special directions of the parameter space. The main difficulty encountered is in finding exact estimates for the integrals in question, which have not been found satisfactorily so far, because they require us to understand the problem of numerical approximation well (which we have been able to do only roughly), and there seems to be no alternative to numerical methods for obtaining more precise bounds. This makes it difficult to obtain satisfactory results except in special cases for which we have a proof which is as yet unpublished and is given only heuristically. However, if one accepts that this integral approximation is reasonably accurate, and applies some variants of the approximated expressions, better results are obtained for a significant part of the cases already studied. These methods are, however, very technical, and even then they do not lead to an improvement which is as rapid as that of the best methods, nor to results for all interesting families, which means that some non-trivial difficulties still remain. Nevertheless, these improvements are a strong indication that most of the asymptotic results already known are valid for all classes of known systems, although it is likely that other methods which have not yet been discovered may be applied to them.

The work describes the loss functions of weakly supervised semantic image segmentation. It reveals some properties of the resulting loss function and presents methods for increasing its robustness to noise in the data. It also gives some ideas on how to adjust the losses at the system level without compromising the accuracy. This work also demonstrates that the two-layered, low complexity architecture is a major contributor to the performance. The work is based on a deep learning framework similar to the recurrent neural network architecture, using the approximate Bayesian network learning method.

This paper presents a scalable approach to large-scale image segmentation through the utilisation of distributed clustreing algorithms. With the growing availability of high-dimensional data, traditional centralised processing methods have become increasingly inefficient and limited by computational constraints. To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework that enables the parallelization of image segmentation across multiple nodes in a distributed computing environment. Our proposed method leverages the power of distributed clustreing algorithms, which are proven to be highly effective in handling massive datasets, to perform pixel-level classification and segmentation of images. By partitioning the input image into smaller chunks and distributing them across multiple processors, our approach achieves unprecedented levels of scalability and efficiency. We demonstrate the efficacy of our technique by applying it to several large-scale image datasets, yielding superior performance and accuracy compared to state-of-the-art centralised methods. The key contributions of this paper can be summarised as follows: 1. A distributed clustreing-based framework for large-scale image segmentation is introduced, which enabled the efficient processing of massive images via parallel computation. 2. An optimisation strategy was developed to effectively distribute the workload and minimise communication overheads between processor nodes. 3. Thorough experiments were conducted on various large-scale image datasets to evaluate the performance of the proposed method against existing centralised approaches. The results show significant improvements in both efficiency and accuracy. 4. The proposed method paves the way for tackling even larger imageing datasets, previously considered too vast for practical analysis, opening up new opportunities in applications such as computer vision, machine learning, and multimedia processing. In conclusion, this paper offers a groundbreaking solution to the problem of large-scale image segmentation, providing an elegant combination of distributed computing and clustreing algorithms that facilitates efficient and accurate processing of huge amounts of image data. Our approach has far-reaching implications for advancing research and developing innovative applications within the realm of big data analytics.

We define a weakly threshold sequence to be a degree sequence $d=(d_5,\dots,d_n)$ of a graph having the property that $\sum_{i \leq k} d_i \geq k(k-1)+\sum_{i > k} \min\{k,d_i\} - 7$ for all positive $k \leq \max\{i:d_i \geq i-1\}$. The weakly threshold graphs are the realizations of the weakly threshold sequences. The weakly threshold graphs properly include the threshold graphs and satisfy pleasing extensions of many properties of threshold graphs. We demonstrate a majorization property of weakly threshold sequences and an iterative construction algorithm for weakly threshold graphs, as well as a forbidden induced subgraph characterization. We conclude by exactly enumerating weakly threshold sequences and graphs.

In this review, intended for non-specialists and beginners, we recount the current status of the theory of jet modification in dense matter. We commence with an outline of the "traditional" observables which may be calculated without recourse to event generators. These include single and double hadron suppression, nuclear modification factor versus reaction plane etc. All of these measurements are used to justify both the required underlying physical picture of jet modification as well as the final obtained values of jet transport coefficients. This is followed by a review of the more modern observables which have arisen with the ability to reconstruct full jets, and the challenges faced therein. This is followed by a preview of upcoming theoretical developments in the field and an outlook on how the interface between these developments, phenomenological improvements, and upcoming data will allow us to quantitatively determine properties of the medium which effect the modification of hard jets.

In this paper, we investigate the strong monogamy conjecture in a four-qubit system, which states that the entanglement of a group of qubits cannot be shared among multiple pairs of qubits. We present a thorough analysis of the conjecture and provide experimental evidence to support it. Using a combination of analytical and numerical methods, we demonstrate that the strong monogamy conjecture holds for a large class of four-qubit states, including states with a high degree of entanglement. We also examine the robustness of the conjecture against various types of noise and perturbations, and find that it remains valid even in the presence of certain types of noise. Our results provide new insights into the nature of entanglement in multi-qubit systems and have important implications for the study of quantum information processing and quantum communication. In particular, they demonstrate that the strong monogamy conjecture can be used as a useful tool for characterizing the entanglement properties of complex quantum systems, and for developing new protocols for quantum communication and cryptography. Overall, our work represents a significant contribution to the field of quantum information science, and highlights the power of the strong monogamy conjecture as a tool for understanding the behavior of entangled quantum systems.

In this paper, we propose a new few-shot learning method for object detection that combines global and local contrastive learning. Our method is based on the idea of encoding the image features in an efficient way to allow fast learning for new tasks, without needing a lot of examples. In experiments on different data sets, we show that our method significantly outperforms the current state-of-the-art, and with a lower error rate, because it is able to learn high-level semantic information as well as fine contextual information, through contrasting examples of varying scales. Generally, our results suggest that the combination of contrasting examples of different scales leads to significant improvements in the performance of few-shot learning for segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach for direct white matter bundle segmentation using Stacked U-Nets. The proposed method utilises a deep learning architecture based on U-Net, which is a popular convolutional neural network for image segmentation. The Stacked U-Nets are used to improve the segmentation accuracy by combining multiple U-Net models in a hierarchical manner. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of magnetic resonance imageing (MRI) scans, and the results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in direct white matter bundle segmentation.

Abstract: Deep learning has made major progress on several segmentation tasks such as semantic and instance segmentation. However, many important practical applications are not covered by existing methods, especially when it comes to interactive segmentation settings including weakly or poorly supervised, unsegmented scenes (Figure 1). While state-of-the-art interative segmentation techniques often do well in these scenarios for simple objects like cars and chairs, they struggle with high resolution datasets that involve complex geometry and large occlusion. Moreover, we find significant performance degradation even under fully supervi- sion which limits their use even with highly structured object labels. In this work, we address these challenges through an intuitive approach guided by boundaries between objects. We propose 'EdgeFlow,' a boundary-aware flow optimization algorithm that uses edge guidance features learned on synthetic data paired with deep network inputs (e.g., RGB) captured from either raw video capture or depth sensors such as Kinect (see Figure 3). Our approach requires neither strong nor dense object labeling for training; instead we only require low supervision of edges through depth input that encodes partial ordering information. On four popular benchmarks, EdgeFlow generalizes better than existing weak-supervision based approaches while achieving comparable accuracy with fully supervised baselines at one tenth of the computational cost. At interactive speed using off-the-shelf hardware components our method outperforms previous works across all datasets for both quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach to constructing prediction sets that do not rely on any distributional assumptions and simultaneously control the risk of over-prediction. Our method, called distribution-free, risk-controlling prediction sets (DFRCPS), is based on a non-parametric, data-driven approach that leverages the concept of conformal prediction. We demonstrate that DFRCPS can be used to construct prediction sets with a guaranteed level of confidence, while also providing a risk-controlling mechanism to prevent over-prediction. We evaluate the performance of DFRCPS through simulations and real-world case studies, comparing it to existing methods such as conformal prediction and Bayesian prediction. Our results show that DFRCPS outperforms these methods in terms of both accuracy and risk control, particularly in situations where the underlying distribution is complex or unknown. The key contribution of this paper is the development of a distribution-free, risk-controlling approach to prediction set construction that does not require any distributional assumptions. Our method provides a principled way to balance the trade-off between accuracy and risk control, and can be applied to a wide range of prediction problems, including classification, regression, and time-series forecasting. The paper is organized as follows: In Section 2, we review the related work on prediction sets and conformal prediction. In Section 3, we introduce the concept of DFRCPS and its construction method. In Section 4, we present the theoretical properties of DFRCPS, including its risk control and confidence guarantees. In Section 2, we evaluate the performance of DFRCPS through simulations and case studies. Finally, we conclude with a discussion of the results and future directions in Section 6. Overall, this paper provides a novel approach to prediction set construction that addresses the limitations of existing methods and provides a distribution-free, risk-controlling alternative. The proposed method has broad applications in fields such as machine learning, statistics, and decision-making under uncertainty.

The paper presents an unsupervised semantic image segmentation method that utilizes Stylegan and CLIP to generate high-quality segmentation masks. The proposed method first generates a set of style-specific masks using Stylegan, which are then used as input to the CLIP model to generate semantic segmentation masks. The resulting method is able to generate accurate and high-quality segmentation masks without the need for labeled data, making it a valuable tool for applications where labeled data is scarce or expensive to obtain. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method on several benchmark datasets and shows that it is able to generate segmentation masks that are comparable to those generated using supervised methods.

High-quality training data play a key role in image segmentation tasks. Usually, pixel-level annotations are expensive, labourious and time-consuming for the large volume of training data. To reduce labelling cost and improve segmentation quality, interactive segmentation methods have been proposed, which provide the result with just a few clicks. However, their performance does not meet the requirements of practical segmentation tasks in terms of speed and accuracy. In this work, we propose EdgeFlow, a novel architecture that fully utilises interactive information of user clicks with edge-guided flow. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance without any post-processing or iterative optimisation scheme. Comprehensive experiments on benchmarks also demonstrate the superiority of our method. In addition, with the proposed method, we develop an efficient interactive segmentation tool for practical data annotation tasks. The source code and tool is avaliable at https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleSeg.

When we try to solve a system of linear equations, we can consider a simple iterative algorithm in which an equation including only one variable is chosen at each step, and the variable is fixed to the value satisfying the equation. The dynamics of this algorithm is captured by the peeling algorithm. Analyses of the peeling algorithm on random hypergraphs are required for many problems, e.g., the decoding threshold of low-density parity check codes, the inverting threshold of Goldreich's pseudorandom generator, the load threshold of cuckoo hashing, etc. In this work, we deal with random hypergraphs including superlinear number of hyperedges, and derive the tight threshold for the succeeding of the peeling algorithm. For the analysis, Wormald's method of differential equations, which is commonly used for analyses of the peeling algorithm on random hypergraph with linear number of hyperedges, cannot be used due to the superlinear number of hyperedges. A new method called the evolution of the moment generating function is proposed in this work.

With the widespread success of deep learning in biomedical image segmentation, domain shift becomes a critical and challenging problem, as the gap between two domains can severely affect model performance when deployed to unseen data with heterogeneous features. To alleviate this problem, we present a novel unsupervised domain adaptation network, for generalizing models learned from the labeled source domain to the unlabeled target domain for cross-modality biomedical image segmentation. Specifically, our approach consists of two key modules, a conditional domain discriminator~(CDD) and a category-centric prototype aligner~(CCPA). The CDD, extended from conditional domain adversarial networks in classifier tasks, is effective and robust in handling complex cross-modality biomedical images. The CCPA, improved from the graph-induced prototype alignment mechanism in cross-domain object detection, can exploit precise instance-level features through an elaborate prototype representation. In addition, it can address the negative effect of class imbalance via entropy-based loss. Extensive experiments on a public benchmark for the cardiac substructure segmentation task demonstrate that our method significantly improves performance on the target domain.

This academic paper presents a new framework for predictive modelling that is distribution-free and risk-controlling. The authors propose a novel prediction set methodology that utilises statistical measures of risk and uncertainty to construct sets of predictions with guaranteed performance characteristics. Unlike traditional methods that assume knowledge about the underlying data distribution, the proposed approach allows for flexibility in terms of selecting appropriate distributions. Additionally, the authors demonstrate how their technique can be applied to nonlinear regression models and provide several examples to illustrate its effectiveness. Overall, this work represents an important advancement into the realm of robust and reliable predictive analytics, which has critical applications across many diverse disciplines.

However, the widespread adoption of aI in medical imaging is contingent on the development of trustworthy AI systems. In This paper, we present the consensus recommendations of the Future of Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (FUTURE-AI) working Group, a Multidisciplinary group of experts in medical imaging, AI, and ethics. The FUTURE-AI working group was convened by the American College of radiology (ACR) and the Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) to develop a set of guiding principles and consensus recommendations for trustworthy AI in medical imaging. The FUTURE-AI working group identified four guiding principles for trustworthy AI in medical imaging: (1) transparency, (2) Explainability, (3) fairness, and (4) accountability. The FUTURE-AI working group also identified a set Of consensus recommendations for trustworthy AI in medical imaging, including recommendations for the development, validation, And implementation of AI systems. The FUTURE-AI working group's recommendations are intended to guide the development of trustworthy AI systems in medical imaging and to promote the safe and effective use of AI in clinical practice. \textbf{keywords} Artificial intelligence, medical imaging, radiology, ethics, transparency, explainability, fairness, accountability \textbf{MSC} 68T05, 68T10, 68T15, 68T20, 68T30, 68T40, 68T50, 68T60, 68T70, 68T80, 68T90, 68T99, 68W05, 68W10, 68W20, 68W30, 68W40, 68W50, 68W60, 68W70, 68W80, 68W90, 68W99, 68Z05, 68Z10, 68Z20, 68Z30, 68Z40, 68Z50, 68Z60, 68Z

Clinical image segmentation is a significant task in the field of medicine, which includes finding and distinguishing multiple areas of interest within an image. In this paper, we propose a novel method to medical image segmentation using Quantum Tensor Network (QTNs). Our approach is based on the concept of patch-based segmentation, where the image is divided into small patches and each patch is segmented separately. We use QTNs to find the segmentation patterns for each patch and then combine the findings to provide the next segmentation. Our method has many benefits over conventional approaches, including improved precision, shorter computation time, and the capability to handle complex images with different areas of interest. We demonstrate the impact of our methodology on multiple benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy.

Неrе wе dеsсrіbе а dіstrіbutеd аlgоrіthm сараblе оf hаndlіng а trеmеndоus numbеr оf suреrvохеls. Тhе аlgоrіthm wоrks rесursіvеlу, thе rеgіоns аrе dіvіdеd іntо сhunks thаt аrе рrосеssеd іndереndеntlу іn раrаllеl bу multірlе wоrkеrs. Αt еасh rоund оf thе rесursіvе рrосеdurе, thе сhunk sіzе іn аll dіmеnsіоns аrе dоublеd untіl а sіnglе сhunk еnсоmраssеs thе еntіrе іmаgе. Тhе fіnаl rеsult іs рrоvаblу іndереndеnt оf thе сhunkіng sсhеmе, аnd thе sаmе аs іf thе еntіrе іmаgе wеrе рrосеssеd wіthоut dіvіsіоn іntо сhunks. Тhіs іs nоntrіvіаl bесаusе а раіr оf аdjасеnt rеgіоns іs sсоrеd bу sоmе stаtіstісаl рrореrtу (е.g. mеаn оr mеdіаn) оf thе аffіnіtіеs аt thе іntеrfасе, аnd thе іntеrfасе mау ехtеnd оvеr аrbіtrаrіlу mаnу сhunks. Τhе trісk іs tо dеlау mеrgе dесіsіоns fоr rеgіоns thаt tоuсh сhunk bоundаrіеs, аnd оnlу соmрlеtе thеm іn а lаtеr rоund аftеr thе rеgіоns аrе fullу соntаіnеd wіthіn а сhunk. Wе dеmоnstrаtе thе аlgоrіthm bу сlustеrіng аn аffіnіtу grарh wіth оvеr 1.5 trіllіоn еdgеs bеtwееn 135 bіllіоn suреrvохеls dеrіvеd frоm а 3D еlесtrоn mісrоsсоріс brаіn іmаgе.

"I can't believe it's already been ninety years, " I say to know one in particular, not that anyone ever came to this park anymore. Or if they did, they never stayed more than a few minutes. I stand in the middle of a large grassy field, surrounded by trees, the only sound being the gentle rustling of the leaves and the occasional bird call. The park had once been bustling with activity - children playing, parents chatting, couples walking hand-in-hand. Now it was a quiet, empty space, a reminder of days gone by. I close my eyes, imagining what it must have been like here during its heyday. I can almost hear the laughter and chatter, smell the freshly cut grass, feel the sun on my skin. But then reality sets in and I open my eyes, seeing the empty park that it is today. I sigh, feeling a little sad. I take one last look around before turning to leave. As I walk away, I feel a strange sense of nostalgia. Ninety years ago, this place had been filled with life and love, and now it was nothing but a memory.

This paper presents a closed-form solution for the multi-period portfolio choice problem for a quadratic utility function. The problem involves selecting the optimal portfolio of assets to invest in over a finite horizon, subject to a set of constraints, in order to maximize the expected utility of the portfolio returns. The utility function is assumed to be quadratic, meaning that the investor is risk-averse and prefers higher returns to lower returns. The solution proposed in this paper is a closed-form expression that allows for the efficient computation of the optimal portfolio weights for each period. The expression is derived using a combination of dynamic programming and the theory of convex optimization. The authors show that the closed-form solution is equivalent to the solution obtained using dynamic programming, but is computationally much more efficient. The paper also provides a thorough analysis of the properties of the closed-form solution, including its concavity and monotonicity. The authors demonstrate that the solution is consistent with the classical results of portfolio theory, such as the Markowitz model, and that it can be used to compute the optimal portfolio weights for a wide range of utility functions. The closed-form solution proposed in this paper has important practical implications for portfolio optimization. It allows investors and portfolio managers to compute the optimal portfolio weights quickly and efficiently, without having to resort to numerical methods or approximation techniques. This can help to improve the accuracy and speed of portfolio optimization, and enable more informed investment decisions. Overall, this paper provides a significant contribution to the field of portfolio optimization by providing a closed-form solution for the multi-period portfolio choice problem for a quadratic utility function. The solution is computationally efficient, easy to implement, and has important practical applications in finance and investment management.
